title: Enterprise Africa Network (EAN) Fellowship Programme Cohort 2 (2026/27): 100 Entrepreneurship Fellowships for African MSMEs
summary: The Enterprise Africa Network (EAN) Fellowship Programme Cohort 2 (2026/27) is a flagship African Union startup acceleration initiative designed to strengthen promising African micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). The programme provides selected entrepreneurs with structured business training, expert mentorship, intellectual property support, market intelligence and opportunities to access markets across Africa and beyond. For its second cohort, the programme will select 100 fellows from across all 55 African Union Member States , with an ambitious target of generating US$2 million in new attributable revenue and creating 500 new jobs . The initiative is implemented by the African Union Commission s Department of Economic Development, Trade, Tourism, Industry and Minerals (ETTIM) and is closely aligned with the objectives of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) . Application deadline: 30 September 2026. Enterprise Africa Network Fellowship 2026/27: Key Details Programme: Enterprise Africa Network (EAN) Fellowship Programme Cohort: Cohort 2 Programme period: 2026/27 Organiser: African Union Commission Implementing department: Department of Economic Development, Trade, Tourism, Industry and Minerals (ETTIM) Type: Startup acceleration and entrepreneurship fellowship Number of fellows: 100 Geographical coverage: All 55 African Union Member States Target beneficiaries: Youth- and women-led small enterprises Minimum business age: 2 years Minimum employees: 3 full-time employees Programme duration: 12 months Application opens: 31 July 2026 Application deadline: 30 September 2026 Results: October 2026 Programme commencement: November 2026 Application: Online Official contact: AUEAN@AfricanUnion.org What Is the Enterprise Africa Network Fellowship? The Enterprise Africa Network Fellowship Programme is an African Union startup acceleration initiative created to support promising African entrepreneurs and strengthen the continent s MSME ecosystem. Rather than focusing only on classroom-based entrepreneurship training, the EAN Fellowship combines several forms of practical business support. Selected fellows receive structured training, access to experienced mentors, market intelligence, intellectual property support and opportunities to connect with potential markets and business partners. The programme is designed around the reality that African businesses often need more than access to capital to grow. Entrepreneurs may also require stronger business strategies, improved knowledge of regional markets, better understanding of intellectual property, access to networks and assistance navigating cross-border trade. EAN therefore seeks to help promising businesses become more competitive and better positioned to take advantage of opportunities created by African economic integration. The first EAN cohort, conducted in 2024/25, trained 56 fellows from 30 African countries and generated more than US$1 million in deals and contracts . Building on that experience, Cohort 2 will expand considerably, with 100 fellows representing all 55 AU Member States . Who Can Apply for the EAN Fellowship? The EAN Fellowship is specifically designed for youth- and women-led small enterprises that meet the programme s business eligibility requirements. To qualify, an enterprise must: Be registered and operating in an African Union Member State . Be formally registered as a business entity . Have been operating for at least two years . Employ a minimum of three full-time staff members . The African Union is particularly encouraging applications from: Women-led enterprises. Enterprises from underrepresented African regions. Businesses from small island AU Member States . The programme is therefore not intended for individuals who simply have a business idea but have not yet established a formally registered and operating enterprise. Applicants should be able to demonstrate that their businesses are already functioning and have reached a level of maturity appropriate for one of the three fellowship tiers. Eligible Countries and Geographic Coverage The Enterprise Africa Network Fellowship is a continental African opportunity . Cohort 2 intends to select fellows from all 55 African Union Member States . This means eligible enterprises can apply from countries across: North Africa West Africa East Africa Central Africa Southern Africa The programme also places specific emphasis on achieving balanced representation across the AU s five continental regions. At least 40 percent of the 100 fellowship places are reserved to ensure representation across all five AU regions. In addition, at least five places are reserved for enterprises from African Union small island Member States . This geographic approach is intended to ensure that the fellowship does not disproportionately benefit businesses from only a small number of African countries or regions. Seven Eligible Business Sectors The EAN Fellowship covers seven sectors , organised into two broad clusters that reflect opportunities connected to intra-African trade and the AfCFTA. Products Cluster The Products Cluster focuses on enterprises producing goods with potential for intra-African trade. 1. Manufacturing Manufacturing businesses can apply under this category. This may include enterprises involved in the production, processing or assembly of goods for African and international markets. The fellowship can provide such businesses with opportunities to strengthen their business models, explore regional markets and develop strategies for expansion. 2. Agro-processing Agro-processing enterprises are also eligible. This sector is particularly relevant to Africa s agricultural value chains because processing agricultural products can increase value addition, create employment and improve opportunities for regional trade. Businesses operating in food processing and other forms of agricultural value addition may therefore find the EAN Fellowship particularly relevant. 3. Creative Industries The Creative Industries category covers businesses operating within Africa s creative economy. Creative enterprises can benefit from business development support, market intelligence, intellectual property knowledge and opportunities to expand their reach beyond domestic markets. Services Cluster The Services Cluster focuses on businesses operating in key service industries. 4. ICT and Digital Technology and digital businesses are eligible to apply. This category reflects the growing role of digital technologies in African economies and the increasing opportunities for technology companies to provide services across borders. 5. Fintech Financial technology businesses are included among the programme s priority sectors. Fintech enterprises are increasingly important to Africa s financial ecosystem, particularly in areas such as digital payments, financial inclusion and technology-enabled financial services. 6. Health Businesses operating in the health sector are also eligible. The programme recognises the importance of strengthening African enterprises that provide innovative products and services addressing healthcare needs across the continent. 7. Logistics and Transport Businesses operating in logistics and transportation can apply. This sector is particularly important for AfCFTA because efficient movement of goods and people is essential to increasing intra-African commerce. Three EAN Fellowship Tiers One of the distinctive features of Cohort 2 is the division of fellows into three tiers based on enterprise maturity . Training, mentorship and market-access support will be tailored to the needs of each tier. Tier Places Enterprise Profile Tier 1 – Growth 35 Operating for 2–5 years, minimum 3 employees and demonstrable market traction Tier 2 – Expansion 40 Operating for 5–10 years, 10–30 employees and cross-border ambition Tier 3 – Scale-Ready 25 Operating for 10+ years or demonstrating an investor-ready profile Understanding these categories is important because applicants should be prepared to demonstrate where their enterprise currently sits in its development journey. Tier 1 – Growth The Growth tier is intended for relatively young enterprises that have already moved beyond the startup stage and demonstrate evidence of market traction. Eligible businesses under this tier should generally: Have operated for 2–5 years . Employ at least three full-time employees . Demonstrate market traction. This tier is particularly relevant to businesses seeking to strengthen their foundations and prepare for the next phase of growth. Tier 2 – Expansion The Expansion tier targets businesses that have established themselves more firmly and are ready to pursue wider markets. Businesses in this category should generally: Have operated for 5–10 years . Employ between 10 and 30 employees . Demonstrate ambitions to expand across borders. The emphasis on cross-border ambition is particularly relevant to the AfCFTA and the EAN s goal of strengthening intra-African trade. Tier 3 – Scale-Ready The Scale-Ready tier is designed for more mature businesses. Enterprises may qualify based on: Operating for 10 years or more , or Having an investor-ready profile . These businesses are expected to have greater capacity for expansion and may be positioned to benefit from more advanced market-access and business-to-business opportunities. What Does the EAN Fellowship Offer? Selected fellows will participate in a 12-month structured programme . The programme combines training, mentorship, market intelligence and business networking. Key components include: 1. Structured Business Training All fellows receive 12 months of structured training across 10 modules . The training is differentiated according to the sector and enterprise tier of each participant. This means the programme is designed to provide more relevant support depending on whether an enterprise is at the growth, expansion or scale-ready stage. 2. Expert Mentorship Fellows receive expert mentorship through African Union partners . Mentorship can help entrepreneurs strengthen their decision-making, identify growth opportunities and address business challenges. For businesses seeking regional expansion, access to experienced mentors can also provide valuable insight into market-entry strategies and cross-border operations. 3. African Trade Observatory Access Participants will gain access to the African Trade Observatory (ATO) and relevant AfCFTA market-intelligence tools. This is an important feature of the fellowship because businesses interested in expanding across Africa need reliable information about potential markets. Market intelligence can help entrepreneurs understand: Regional market opportunities. Trade trends. Potential markets for their products or services. Cross-border opportunities. Business expansion possibilities. 4. Continental Events Fellows will participate in continental events, providing opportunities to engage with entrepreneurs, experts, institutions and potential business partners from different African markets. Such events can contribute to business networking and collaboration. Market Access Opportunities Market access is a major component of the EAN Fellowship. The programme is not limited to training entrepreneurs. It is also designed to help participating businesses explore opportunities beyond their domestic markets. Tier 1 and Tier 2 Market-Entry Sessions Fellows in Tiers 1 and 2 will participate in virtual market-entry sessions covering 10 AfCFTA pilot countries . These sessions are intended to expose businesses to potential markets and help entrepreneurs better understand the process of entering new African markets. Tier 3 B2B Matchmaking Tier 3 fellows will participate in business-to-business matchmaking sessions . These sessions are designed to create opportunities for mature enterprises to connect with potential business partners, customers and other commercial stakeholders. For scale-ready businesses, B2B matchmaking may be particularly valuable for developing commercial relationships and expanding regional operations. EAN Fellowship and the African Continental Free Trade Area The EAN Fellowship is closely connected to the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) . The AfCFTA is intended to strengthen economic integration across Africa and create a larger single market for goods and services. For African MSMEs, greater continental integration can create opportunities to: Enter new African markets. Expand customer bases. Build regional supply chains. Establish cross-border partnerships. Increase exports. Develop new products and services. Create employment. The EAN Fellowship seeks to help entrepreneurs develop the capabilities and connections necessary to take advantage of these opportunities. Application Process Applications for the EAN Fellowship are submitted online. Applicants will be required to provide information about their enterprise, including: Business registration details. Business sector. Number of years the enterprise has operated. Number of employees. Countries where the business currently trades. Revenue range. Intellectual property status. Access to formal finance. Applicants will also need to submit a written pitch of up to 800 words . The pitch should explain: What the enterprise does. The main challenge facing the business. What the applicant hopes to achieve through participation in the EAN Fellowship. Applicants should use the pitch to clearly communicate the enterprise s current position, growth potential and reasons for seeking support through the programme. APPLY HERE Supporting Financial Document A supporting document verifying access to finance is not required at the initial application stage . However, shortlisted applicants will later be asked to provide evidence of access to formal finance. Acceptable evidence may include: Bank statement. Mobile money statement. Equivalent financial documentation. Applicants should therefore ensure that appropriate financial records are available should they progress to the shortlisting stage. Important Warning About False Information Applicants should take particular care when completing the application. The African Union states that misrepresentation of any information provided in the application will result in immediate disqualification and permanent ineligibility for all future EAN Fellowship cohorts . Applicants should therefore ensure that: Business registration information is accurate. Employee numbers are truthful. Revenue information is accurate. Years of operation are correctly stated. Trading countries are accurately reported. Financial information is supported by legitimate documentation. All other information submitted can be verified where necessary. Applicants should not exaggerate the size, revenue, age or performance of their enterprise in an attempt to qualify for a higher tier. Who Is Not Eligible? Certain individuals and organisations are explicitly excluded from applying. The following are not eligible : Current staff of the African Union Commission. Former staff of the African Union Commission. Employees and representatives of EAN institutional partners. Staff members of Regional Economic Communities (RECs). Graduates of any previous EAN Fellowship cohort. Applicants who fall into any of these categories should not submit an application. Key Dates for the EAN Fellowship 2026/27 Applicants should keep the following dates in mind: Stage Date Applications open 31 July 2026 Application deadline 30 September 2026 Results communicated October 2026 Programme begins November 2026 The application deadline is 30 September 2026 . Applicants are strongly advised to submit before the final day to avoid technical problems or incomplete applications. Visit HERE to learn more about the Enterprise Africa Network (EAN) Fellowship Programme Cohort 2. How to Apply for the Enterprise Africa Network Fellowship Interested entrepreneurs should follow these steps: Step 1: Confirm eligibility Check that your enterprise: Operates in an AU Member State. Is formally registered. Has operated for at least two years. Has at least three full-time employees. Falls within one of the seven eligible sectors. Is youth- or women-led. Does not fall under any of the excluded categories. Step 2: Identify your enterprise tier Determine whether your business fits: Tier 1 – Growth Tier 2 – Expansion Tier 3 – Scale-Ready Be realistic when determining your enterprise s maturity. Step 3: Gather your business information Prepare accurate information concerning registration, employees, revenue, markets, intellectual property and access to finance. Step 4: Prepare the 800-word pitch Clearly explain your enterprise, its main market challenge and what you want to achieve through the fellowship. Step 5: Review your application Carefully check every answer before submitting. Incorrect or misleading information can lead to disqualification and permanent ineligibility for future cohorts. Step 6: Submit online Use the official EAN Fellowship application form . How to Strengthen Your EAN Fellowship Application Entrepreneurs should avoid treating the application as simply another business registration form. The programme is competitive, with only 100 fellowship places available. A stronger application should clearly communicate: A clear business model Explain what your company sells or provides, who its customers are and how it generates revenue. Evidence of market traction Where relevant, provide credible information demonstrating that customers are already using or purchasing your products or services. A clearly defined challenge Do not simply state that your business needs funding. Explain the specific market, operational, technical, regulatory or expansion challenge you are facing. A strong growth strategy Explain where you want the business to go and how the EAN Fellowship can help you get there. Regional ambitions If you intend to expand into other African countries, clearly explain which markets you are considering and why. Alignment with AfCFTA Show that you understand how your business can contribute to or benefit from increased intra-African trade. Accurate information Every figure and statement should be truthful and, where necessary, verifiable. Why This Fellowship Could Be Valuable for African Entrepreneurs African MSMEs play a major role in employment, innovation and economic development across the continent. However, many businesses face challenges when attempting to move from local operations to regional or international markets. The EAN Fellowship addresses several of these challenges through a combination of: Business training. Mentorship. Market intelligence. Networking. Market-entry support. B2B matchmaking. Intellectual property support. Continental exposure. The programme s focus on different enterprise maturity levels is also significant. A two-year-old business with three employees may require very different support from a ten-year-old enterprise preparing for investment or regional expansion. By separating participants into three tiers, the programme aims to provide more targeted support. Official Application and Programme Resources Apply for the EAN Fellowship Read the official African Union call for applications Download the official EAN Call for Applications Download the EAN Concept Note Contact: AUEAN@AfricanUnion.org Conclusion The Enterprise Africa Network Fellowship Programme Cohort 2 (2026/27) represents a major opportunity for ambitious African entrepreneurs seeking to grow their businesses, access new markets and build stronger connections across the continent. With 100 fellowship places available across all 55 African Union Member States , the programme combines 12 months of structured training with expert mentorship, AfCFTA market intelligence, continental networking and targeted market-access opportunities. The three-tier structure also allows businesses at different stages of development to receive support suited to their level of maturity, from growing enterprises with demonstrated market traction to established businesses preparing for regional expansion or investment. Entrepreneurs who meet the eligibility requirements should begin preparing their business information and 800-word pitch early. Most importantly, applicants should ensure that every piece of information submitted is accurate, as misrepresentation can result in permanent exclusion from future EAN Fellowship cohorts. Application deadline: 30 September 2026. This is an opportunity for African businesses not only to strengthen their individual enterprises but also to contribute to a more integrated, competitive and interconnected African economy. title: Apple MBA Internships 2026: Explore Graduate-Level Opportunities Across AI, Marketing, Supply Chain, Retail and Product Operations
summary: Apple is inviting qualified graduate students to express interest in its MBA internship opportunities in the United States , offering potential pathways into a wide range of business, technology, operations, marketing, retail, analytics, and supply chain functions. The opportunity is designed for students pursuing an MBA or relevant master’s degree who want to gain exposure to complex, cross-functional projects within one of the world’s most recognized technology companies. The Apple MBA internship posting was published on August 5, 2026 , under Role Number 200676091-3810 . Importantly, Apple states that this posting is not for one specific job opening. Instead, candidates who submit their resumes are expressing interest in being contacted about this type of role at Apple in the future. Opportunity Overview The Apple MBA internship opportunity provides graduate students with the possibility of being considered for roles across several major business and operational areas. These include artificial intelligence and machine learning, AppleCare, Apple Services, manufacturing design, marketing, product operations, retail, strategic sourcing, and supply chain operations. The breadth of the opportunity makes it particularly relevant to students whose career interests extend beyond traditional MBA functions. Depending on the area, interns may work on strategy, product management, analytics, procurement, operations, supply chain planning, marketing, business process improvement, customer experience, sourcing, or program management. AI and Machine Learning EPM One of the areas highlighted in the Apple MBA internship posting is AI/ML EPM . Apple explains that its machine learning and artificial intelligence teams are developing experiences that are integrated into its products. The company combines hardware and software capabilities across its devices, allowing research and engineering teams to collaborate closely while focusing on user experience and data protection. For MBA candidates interested in technology strategy, product development, artificial intelligence, and cross-functional management, this area provides exposure to the business side of emerging technologies. AppleCare Opportunities The internship opportunities also extend to AppleCare , with several different functional areas identified in the posting. Contact Center Operations Interns and professionals working in Contact Center Operations support Apple’s business and operational needs through technology and strategic approaches. Responsibilities can involve monitoring service levels and contact-center volumes while supporting broader AppleCare business objectives. Field Service Channel Management The Field Service Channel Manager function focuses on improving customer satisfaction while reducing operational costs. This involves reengineering processes and policies and working with Apple Authorized Service Providers and mobile carriers to develop service programs aligned with Apple’s business objectives and customer needs. Global Repair Center The Global Repair Center area focuses on the operations of Apple’s expanding network of repair centers and its reverse supply chain. This work involves managing complex repair operations within a growing global network. Online and Digital Support Online and Digital Support focuses on creating digital content and solutions that improve the Apple customer experience. The work can involve developing self-service learning solutions across websites, applications, social platforms, search optimization, and machine learning. Procurement AppleCare procurement involves managing supplier relationships, sourcing optimization, and planning activities connected to repair strategies, costs, supply continuity, and capacity. Reporting and Analytics The Reporting and Analytics function uses AppleCare business data to generate strategic recommendations and operational insights. The posting specifically highlights translating business needs into analytical requirements and applying advanced quantitative analysis. Supply Chain Management AppleCare Supply Chain Management involves building and operating global reverse supply chains and optimizing areas such as forecasting, purchasing, inventory management, repair planning, warranty redemption, and supply chain projects. Apple Services MBA internship opportunities are also available within Apple Services . Apple’s services portfolio includes products and platforms such as Apple Music, Apple News, Apple Podcasts, Apple TV, Apple TV+, Apple Pay, Apple Card, Maps, Search Ads, iCloud, and productivity and creativity applications. The Services opportunities can span areas including: Software engineering Data science and analytics Quality assurance Marketing Business development Other business and technology functions This makes the Services track potentially attractive to MBA students interested in the intersection of technology, customer experience, digital products, data, and commercial strategy. Manufacturing Design Another area available through the MBA internship posting is Manufacturing Design , particularly the Global Supply Manager function. Global Supply Managers are responsible for commercial relationships with manufacturing partners, including cost negotiations, risk management, and operational and cost efficiencies. The role also involves balancing business and engineering priorities during product development and launch. The function works closely with operations, supply quality, engineering, and product and industrial design teams. It can therefore provide an environment in which MBA candidates interested in manufacturing, sourcing, operations, and product development can apply business and strategic skills in a highly technical setting. Marketing and Product Management Apple’s Product Marketing group is another important area highlighted in the internship opportunity. The role involves guiding product positioning from concept through development and launch, using customer insights to inform product-development decisions and helping turn ideas into products that resonate with customers. Apple also notes that it combines product management and product marketing responsibilities into a cross-functional Product Management role. These teams collaborate with functions, including: Design Engineering Finance Legal Marketing communications Public relations Market research Sales Customer support This cross-functional structure makes the opportunity particularly relevant to MBA students interested in product strategy, marketing, customer insights, business development, and organizational leadership. Product Operations MBA internship opportunities are also available in Product Operations , including Operations Program Manager and Product Quality Manager functions. Operations Program Manager Operations Program Managers work with New Product Introduction or Sustaining Operations teams on product readiness, product launches, and programs extending through the end of a product’s life cycle. The role involves product manufacturability, testability, responsiveness, quality, cost, and flexibility. Apple identifies several capabilities associated with successful operations program management, including: Program and project management Clear communication across organizational levels Facilitating actions Resolving conflicts Managing through relationships and influence Maintaining control in high-intensity projects Product Quality Manager Product Quality Managers are responsible for final product quality and play a leadership role within operations technical teams during product development and production. The role connects engineering and operations while requiring an understanding of both technical issues and their broader business implications. Product Quality Managers can also be involved in contract manufacturer preparation, validation, product transfers, and operational innovations designed to improve production quality, capacity, and efficiency. Retail Opportunities Apple’s Retail corporate team is another area available to MBA interns. According to the posting, Apple Retail develops strategies, drives initiatives, and builds technologies supporting millions of visitors across its global e-commerce operations and more than 450 stores worldwide. MBA interns may take on roles comparable to the following: Program Manager Product Manager Business Analyst Merchandising Manager Operations Manager The areas mentioned include Central Operations, E-Commerce, Merchandising, Real Estate, and Sales Service. For MBA students interested in retail strategy, customer experience, operations, digital commerce, or business analytics, this represents one of the broader areas within the Apple internship posting. Strategic Sourcing The Strategic Sourcing track includes opportunities such as Global Supply Manager, Operations Product Development and Materials Program Manager. Global Supply Manager Global Supply Managers work between Apple and industries supplying core component technologies. Their responsibilities include developing sourcing strategies, evaluating technology-driven product innovations, and considering factors such as market dynamics, competitive behavior, negotiation, pricing, manufacturing processes, and risk mitigation. Operations Product Development Operations Product Development teams advise development teams on operational, cost and supply chain considerations. Operations Product Managers work with technologies from cost, supply chain and technical perspectives; manage product costs against targets; and collaborate with Global Supply Managers on supplier planning. Materials Program Manager Materials Program Managers work with supply chain partners to address supply constraints while considering demand priorities, factory capacity, logistics, quality, and materials flow throughout Apple’s multi-tier supply chain. The function supports supply availability across the product life cycle while seeking to optimize supply and minimize excess and obsolete inventory. Supply Chain Operations Apple’s MBA internship opportunity also covers Supply Chain Operations , including Supply Demand Management and Business Process Re-engineering. Supply Demand Management The Supply Demand Planner role involves forecasting product demand, analyzing production requirements, allocating global supply across distribution channels, and influencing quarterly sales projections. The role requires collaboration across multiple Apple teams to develop strategy and drive execution throughout the global supply chain. Business Process Re-engineering Business Process Re-engineering focuses on sophisticated global initiatives designed to develop and implement technology and business-process solutions. The goal is to increase efficiency, improve customer satisfaction, challenge existing approaches, and build capabilities that provide deeper business insight, accelerate decision-making, and support automation. Who Is Eligible for the Apple MBA Internships? The primary eligibility requirement is clearly stated by Apple. Applicants must be currently pursuing an MBA or a master’s degree in supply chain, engineering, operations management, or a related field . There is also an important academic-status requirement. By the end of the internship, the student must either: Return to school to continue their education; or Have the internship constitute the final requirement needed to graduate. Preferred Qualifications Apple lists several additional qualifications as helpful, although it explicitly states that they are not requirements . These include: Strategic and detail-oriented thinking Strong problem-solving and issue-resolution abilities Ability to influence cross-functional team members Ability to adapt to dynamic and rapidly changing environments Excellent analytical skills Excellent communication skills Ability to work through complex details and develop clear strategies and plans These preferred qualities reflect the cross-functional nature of the internship opportunities, where candidates may need to combine analytical thinking, communication, problem-solving, and strategic decision-making. Countries, Race, and Geographic Eligibility The Apple posting identifies the opportunity under United States Students and places the posting within Apple’s United States careers listings. However, the supplied Apple posting does not specify a particular citizenship requirement, nationality restriction, race requirement, or list of eligible countries or continents . Apple explicitly states that it is an equal opportunity employer and that it seeks to provide equal opportunity without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or other legally protected characteristics. Therefore, applicants should not assume that a particular race, ethnicity, or nationality is required based solely on this posting. Candidates should review the official application process and any applicable employment or work-authorization requirements before submitting their applications. Is There an Application Deadline? There is no fixed application deadline stated in the Apple posting . Instead, Apple states that it accepts applications to this posting on an ongoing basis . This means interested candidates should not wait for a conventional closing date. Because the posting is intended to identify candidates who may be contacted about this type of role in the future, submitting a strong resume as early as possible can be important. Deadline: Ongoing / no specific closing date stated. Important Note About the Application This opportunity should not be interpreted as a single internship vacancy with one fixed job description. Apple explicitly explains that the posting is not for a specific job opening . By submitting a resume, candidates are expressing interest in being contacted about this type of role at Apple in the future. Consequently, applicants should ensure that their resumes clearly communicate their MBA or relevant master’s background, career interests, technical and analytical capabilities, leadership experience, and relevant professional achievements. How to Apply for the Apple MBA Internship Opportunity Interested candidates can submit their resumes through Apple’s official careers application system. Candidates should carefully review the official posting and ensure that their academic status meets Apple’s requirements before submitting their resume. APPLY HERE Why This Opportunity Is Relevant to MBA Students The Apple MBA internship opportunity stands out because of the unusually broad range of functions covered by the posting. Rather than limiting graduate interns to conventional business functions, Apple identifies opportunities spanning technology, artificial intelligence, customer service, digital services, manufacturing, marketing, product management, retail, sourcing, and global supply chain operations. For students pursuing careers in business and technology, this breadth can make the opportunity particularly relevant to different professional interests. A candidate with strong analytical skills may be suited to reporting, analytics, or supply-demand planning, while someone interested in product strategy may be more interested in marketing or product management. Candidates with supply chain interests can explore strategic sourcing, materials management, manufacturing design, or supply chain operations. The cross-functional nature of the roles also means that communication, influence, analytical reasoning, and problem-solving are emphasized alongside academic qualifications. What Applicants Should Highlight Although Apple does not require the preferred qualifications listed in the posting, applicants can strengthen their applications by demonstrating evidence of capabilities that align with the internship areas. Relevant experience may include: Business strategy and strategic planning Product management or product marketing Data analysis and business intelligence Supply chain management Procurement and sourcing Operations management Project and program management Process improvement Customer experience Digital products and services Market research Cross-functional collaboration Quantitative analysis Problem-solving Communication and stakeholder management The strongest application should connect the candidate’s academic background and professional experience with the type of work they hope to pursue at Apple. Visit HERE for more information about the Apple MBA Internships 2026. Conclusion The Apple MBA Internships 2026 opportunity provides graduate students with the chance to express interest in a broad range of potential internship roles across one of the world’s leading technology companies. With opportunities spanning AI and machine learning, AppleCare, Apple Services, manufacturing design, marketing, product operations, retail, strategic sourcing and supply chain operations, the posting offers multiple pathways for students with different business and technical interests. The opportunity is particularly suited to students currently pursuing an MBA or a relevant master’s degree who can demonstrate strong analytical, communication, strategic-thinking, problem-solving, and cross-functional collaboration abilities. Since Apple accepts applications on an ongoing basis and does not provide a fixed closing date, eligible students interested in being considered should review the official posting and submit their resumes through Apple’s careers platform. For students seeking exposure to technology-driven business strategy, operations, product development, marketing, retail, sourcing, or global supply chain management, this Apple internship posting represents a significant opportunity to place their graduate education in a highly cross-functional corporate environment. title: European Youth Foundation Grants 2027: Council of Europe Opens €850,000 Funding Call for International Youth Projects
summary: The European Youth Foundation of the Council of Europe has opened two major calls for proposals to support international youth cooperation activities and long-term youth projects taking place from 2027 onwards. Through a combined indicative budget of €850,000, the Foundation intends to support approximately 20 international youth initiatives addressing democracy, human rights, inclusion, peacebuilding, youth participation and the development of youth work. The two funding opportunities are: International one-off youth cooperation activities in 2027, offering grants of up to €25,000. International long-term youth cooperation projects in 2027, offering grants of up to €60,000. These opportunities are intended for eligible youth-led non-governmental organisations rather than individual applicants. Organisations must be registered and validated in the European Youth Foundation’s online system before they can submit a proposal. The officially advertised application deadline for both calls is 1 October 2026 at 23:59 CET . Applications must be submitted through the Support4Youth online grant-management platform . The official announcement was published by the European Youth Foundation on 17 August 2026 . European Youth Foundation Grants 2027: Key Information Funding organisation: European Youth Foundation Parent institution: Council of Europe Funding year: 2027 Number of open calls: Two Combined indicative budget: €850,000 Maximum one-off activity grant: €25,000 Maximum long-term project grant: €60,000 Indicative number of grants: Approximately 10 under each call Eligible applicants: Qualifying youth-led non-governmental organisations and networks registered with the European Youth Foundation Application languages: English or French Submission method: Online through Support4Youth Application deadline: 1 October 2026 at 23:59 CET Assessment period: 2 October–15 November 2026 Final grant decisions: 14–15 December 2026 Notification of results: 16–18 December 2026 Expected grant agreements: Early January 2027 Co-financing: Required through financial, human-resource or in-kind contributions What Is the European Youth Foundation? The European Youth Foundation, commonly known as the EYF, is a Council of Europe fund that provides financial support to youth organisations working with and for young people. Established in 1972, the Foundation supports youth-led initiatives that promote peace, international understanding, cooperation, democracy, human rights and fundamental freedoms. The Foundation works with youth organisations that are non-governmental, non-profit, voluntary and participatory. Its funding is designed to strengthen young people’s involvement in democratic societies and help youth organisations organise educational, advocacy, awareness-raising, cooperation and capacity-building activities. The Council of Europe is separate from the European Union. It currently has 46 member states and focuses on democracy, human rights and the rule of law. Youth organisations seeking EYF support must generally be established in one of those 46 member states. The European Youth Foundation explains its mandate and relationship with the Council of Europe on its official website . Overview of the Two EYF Calls for Proposals Feature One-Off Youth Cooperation Activities Long-Term Youth Cooperation Projects Call reference 2027.C5.A 2027.C6.B Maximum grant €25,000 €60,000 Indicative total budget €250,000 €600,000 Intended number of grants 10 10 Main format One principal international youth meeting A combination of international meetings and other activities Project period 1 January–31 December 2027 Up to 18 months Required start date Not before 1 January 2027 Between 1 January and 31 March 2027 Latest possible completion 31 December 2027 30 September 2028 International meeting requirement Normally at least four programme days At least one meeting of four programme days Main applicant types International, sub-regional and qualifying national youth NGOs or networks International youth NGOs and international youth NGO networks Reporting deadline Within two months of completion and no later than 29 February 2028 Within two months of completion and no later than 30 November 2028 Call One: International One-Off Youth Cooperation Activities in 2027 The first opportunity is the Call for Proposals for International One-Off Youth Cooperation Activities in 2027, identified as 2027.C5.A . This call supports international meetings that bring young people from different countries together to learn, exchange ideas, build cooperation and address issues connected with the Council of Europe’s youth priorities. Objectives of the One-Off Activities Call Projects should contribute to one or more of the following objectives: Enhance young people’s participation in democratic societies, youth organisations and other forms of civic mobilisation and action. Give young people the opportunity to explore an important subject connected with EYF funding priorities and the challenges they experience in different contexts. Promote intercultural dialogue by enabling young people from different cultures to meet, cooperate, network and learn from one another. Build capacity for future action and inspire educational, advocacy, cooperation and awareness-raising initiatives. Activities That May Be Supported The main activity should be an international meeting of young people. Possible formats include: Youth camps Seminars Conferences Training courses Study visits Strategic meetings Advocacy meetings Other comparable international youth activities This list is illustrative rather than exhaustive. A grant may support one main international meeting together with its preparatory and follow-up or evaluation meetings. The project must be developed and implemented by a multicultural project team. It should follow Council of Europe quality standards and use approaches such as: Non-formal education Intercultural learning Meaningful youth participation Human rights education Inclusive and participatory learning methods Minimum Duration of the International Meeting The main international meeting should normally last for at least four programme days. Arrival and departure days are not counted as programme or working days. Applicants must show the number of actual working days in their narrative application. Project Implementation Period The full project period may begin no earlier than 1 January 2027 and must finish by 31 December 2027. Applicants must include the complete duration of the initiative, covering: Preparation The main international activity Evaluation Follow-up work The period during which project costs are incurred Projects completed before the application is submitted will be automatically excluded. Participant Requirements The activity must involve participants: Residing in at least seven Council of Europe member states With adequate representation among the participating countries Of whom at least 75% are no older than 30 With attention to the participation of young people with disabilities With specific consideration for gender equality and social inclusion Participants from countries outside the Council of Europe may be included where their involvement is properly justified. This does not remove the requirement to involve participants residing in at least seven Council of Europe member states. Maximum Funding and Available Budget Applicants may request up to €25,000 . The total indicative budget for the call is €250,000 , and the European Youth Foundation intends to award approximately 10 grants. The Foundation is not obliged to award the entire available budget or exactly 10 grants. It may award fewer grants or redistribute funds depending on the number and quality of eligible applications. Full conditions are available in the official overview for Call 2027.C5.A . Organisations Eligible for the One-Off Activities Call The applicant must be registered in the European Youth Foundation grant system under one of the following categories: An international non-governmental youth organisation. An international network of non-governmental youth organisations. A sub-regional network of non-governmental youth organisations. A national non-governmental youth organisation working with at least three national youth NGO partners from three other Council of Europe member states. A national non-governmental youth organisation working with an international non-governmental youth organisation or international network as a partner. In a partnership involving several organisations, only one eligible organisation submits the application on behalf of the partnership. A national youth organisation applying through the first partnership route therefore needs at least three eligible partners in three other countries, creating a partnership of at least four national youth organisations. Call Two: International Long-Term Youth Cooperation Projects in 2027 The second opportunity is the Call for Proposals for International Long-Term Youth Cooperation Projects in 2027, identified as 2027.C6.B . This funding stream is intended for organisations that want to implement a strategic, multi-activity project rather than organise only one international meeting. Objectives of the Long-Term Projects Call Projects should address several of the following objectives: Contribute to the strategic development of the applicant organisation, its members and its networks. Build institutional capacity and knowledge hubs within youth organisations. Develop and use new tools, manuals, research, educational materials or policy outputs. Establish lasting strategic partnerships and cross-border cooperation between young people and youth organisations. Strengthen young people’s knowledge and skills in areas connected with the EYF funding priorities. Reach young people at local, national and international levels through multiplier activities. Support educational, advocacy, awareness-raising and cooperation initiatives with a wider and more sustainable impact. Activities That May Be Included A long-term project should combine international meetings with other complementary activities. These may include: Training courses Youth seminars and conferences Advocacy projects Public-awareness campaigns Research Policy development Production of manuals and educational resources Online learning resources Local youth activities Regional initiatives Communication campaigns Multiplier activities Development of websites, videos or podcasts Support for youth-led follow-up initiatives At least one project activity must be an international youth meeting lasting at least four programme days. The project must be implemented by a multicultural team and use Council of Europe youth-sector approaches such as non-formal education, youth participation, intercultural learning and human rights education. What Is a Multiplier Activity? A multiplier activity takes knowledge, skills or content developed through the main project and shares it with a wider group of young people. It may take the form of: Workshops Advocacy meetings Community debates Campaign activities Local training sessions Awareness-raising events Follow-up activities organised by participants or partner organisations Multiplier activities should have clearly defined objectives and involve several young people directly. They must also be properly documented and reported. Duration and Implementation Period Long-term projects may last for a maximum of 18 months . The project must begin between: 1 January 2027; and 31 March 2027. The latest permitted project completion date is 30 September 2028. The application should cover the complete period from the official start date until all activities are completed and all eligible costs have been incurred. Participant Requirements Across the majority of project activities, participants should: Reside in at least seven Council of Europe member states Represent participating countries in appropriate numbers Include at least 75% of people who are no older than 30 Include young people with disabilities Reflect gender equality and social inclusion considerations Participants from non-member countries may be involved where this is relevant and properly justified. Maximum Funding and Available Budget Applicants may request up to €60,000 . The indicative budget available under the call is €600,000 , and the European Youth Foundation intends to award approximately 10 grants. The Foundation may decide not to award all available funding or may redistribute the budget depending on the quality and number of proposals received. Full requirements are available in the official overview for Call 2027.C6.B . Organisations Eligible for the Long-Term Projects Call Eligibility for the long-term project call is narrower than for the one-off activities call. Only the following may apply: An international non-governmental youth organisation; or An international network of non-governmental youth organisations. National youth organisations and sub-regional networks cannot apply independently for the long-term project call unless they form part of an eligible international organisation or network led by an organisation that meets the call’s requirements. European Youth Foundation Funding Priorities Every proposal must contribute meaningfully to one or more Council of Europe youth-sector priorities. Adding a broad reference to democracy or human rights is not enough. Applicants must explain how their activities, methods and expected results address a relevant priority. The four priorities are detailed on the official EYF Youth Sector Priorities page . 1. Revitalising Pluralistic Democracy Relevant projects may address: Young people’s freedom of association and right to assemble Participation in political and public decision-making Barriers preventing young people from participating in democratic processes Civic space for youth organisations Artificial intelligence and internet governance Young people’s awareness of the democratic implications of artificial intelligence Local decision-making involving young people Participation of rural youth, minorities and vulnerable groups Climate change, environmental degradation and the right to a healthy environment 2. Young People’s Access to Rights Relevant areas include: Human rights education Media literacy for children and young people Advocacy for young people’s access to rights Social rights of young people from disadvantaged neighbourhoods Access to services and opportunities Practical implementation of Council of Europe recommendations concerning youth rights 3. Living Together in Peaceful and Inclusive Societies Projects may focus on: Combating discrimination, racism and exclusion Roma youth participation and action against antigypsyism Social inclusion of young refugees Multiple and intersectional discrimination Gender equality Sexual orientation and gender identity Disability inclusion Intercultural dialogue Peacebuilding and conflict transformation Cooperation with neighbouring and other world regions Participation of young people in rural communities Mental health and well-being Support for young people in and from war zones 4. Youth Work Projects may address: Advocacy for youth work Recognition and quality development of youth work Non-formal education and learning Capacity building for youth organisations Professional and institutional development of youth work Strengthening youth work in conflict areas and war zones General Requirements for Applicant Organisations All applicants must first be registered and validated by the European Youth Foundation. To qualify for EYF registration, an organisation should generally: Be non-governmental Be non-profit Have its own statute and governance rules Demonstrate democratic governance Have youth participation built into its decision-making Focus primarily on youth-related activities Work for and with young people Be managed by young people in relation to its programmes and budget Have a vast majority of members between 15 and 30 years old Operate in line with Council of Europe values Be legally established in one of the 46 Council of Europe member states An international youth organisation must normally have at least seven member or affiliated youth organisations operating in seven different Council of Europe member states. An international network must similarly bring together at least seven eligible youth organisations from seven member states and demonstrate sustained cooperation, shared governance and active participation by its members. A sub-regional network generally consists of four to six youth organisations based in different Council of Europe member states within a particular European sub-region. Financial and Operational Capacity In addition to being an eligible youth organisation, the applicant must: Have a bank account capable of receiving payments in euros Demonstrate stable and sufficient financial capacity Be able to continue operating throughout the grant period Contribute to the project through its own or third-party resources Have sufficient staff and volunteers Demonstrate appropriate professional and operational capacity Show relevant experience among the organisation, partners and project team Be capable of managing the grant and completing the required reporting The Council of Europe retains discretion to determine whether an organisation has sufficient financial, operational and professional capacity for the complexity of the proposed project. Registration With the European Youth Foundation Organisations that are not registered must create an account and submit a registration request through Support4Youth . Registration may take up to two weeks. It is not enough to submit a registration request before the deadline: the registration must be reviewed and validated by the EYF Secretariat before 1 October 2026. Organisations should therefore begin registration well in advance. Registration documentation generally includes: The organisation’s original statute An English or French translation if the statute is written in another language Proof of registration issued by a public authority A recent report describing the organisation’s activities A bank statement proving that the organisation has a bank account The EYF registration process is a due-diligence exercise confirming that the applicant is a genuine youth-led, non-governmental and non-profit organisation. Participant Age and International Representation The European Youth Foundation generally defines young people as individuals between 15 and 30 years old. For both calls, at least 75% of participants must not be older than 30. The application forms require applicants to estimate participants within the following age groups: Younger than 15 Between 15 and 30 Older than 30 Project-team members should not be counted as participants. International activities must involve residents of at least seven Council of Europe member states. Applicants must provide credible and balanced country representation rather than adding countries only to meet the numerical requirement. Cross-Cutting Standards EYF-supported projects should be planned by, for and with young people. Applications should also explain how the project will address: Youth participation Gender equality Human rights Social inclusion Discrimination and marginalisation Accessibility for young people with disabilities Environmental responsibility Child safeguarding Ethics and personal dignity Protection from harassment Data protection and privacy Safe and respectful participation Projects should demonstrate these considerations through practical methods, participant recruitment, accessibility arrangements, project-team composition, content and evaluation. Activities the EYF Will Not Fund The following activities are ineligible: Commercial or profit-making operations Purchase of land or buildings Construction or renovation of buildings Purchase of fixed equipment for buildings Tourism activities Scholarships Sports events and competitions School exchanges Activities forming part of a school or university programme Strictly vocational activities Statutory meetings of youth organisations Projects unrelated to Council of Europe work or priorities Activities that do not create space to explore Council of Europe standards, methods, approaches or resources Projects completed before the application is submitted are also ineligible. This means the funding should not be presented as support for tourism, individual education, routine organisational governance or a commercial event. It must support a genuine youth-cooperation project with a clear educational, democratic, human-rights or youth-work purpose. The official EYF grant page provides further guidance on eligible and excluded activities . Co-Financing Requirements The EYF does not fund projects on the assumption that the Foundation will be the only contributor. Every grantee must contribute through its own resources or obtain support from third parties. Co-financing may include: Direct financial contributions Staff time Volunteer time Donated venues or services Other human resources In-kind contributions Contributions from project partners Other approved funding sources The official call does not establish a universal minimum co-financing percentage. However, the budget must clearly distinguish costs requested from the EYF from costs covered by the applicant, partners or other sources. Grant Payment and Reporting For both calls, approved funding is paid in two stages: First instalment: 80% is paid after the grant agreement has been signed by the grantee organisation and the European Youth Foundation. Final balance: The remaining amount is paid after the Council of Europe receives and accepts the final narrative and financial reports. The grantee must submit both reports within two months of the project’s completion. For one-off activities, reporting must be completed no later than 29 February 2028. For long-term projects, reporting must be completed no later than 30 November 2028. Failure to provide acceptable reports may delay the final payment or result in a request to reimburse unsupported or ineligible expenditure. Application Documents A complete application must contain: A completed narrative application form. A completed budget form showing: Costs requested from the European Youth Foundation Costs covered by the applicant Partner contributions Other funding or in-kind contributions Applications must be submitted in English or French. Incomplete applications will not be considered. Information Required for One-Off Activity Applications The one-off activity narrative application asks for: Project Identification Project contact person Email address Telephone number Project title Venue or venues Countries where activities will take place Full project start and end dates Number of programme days Proposal Overview Applicants have a limit of 3,600 characters to explain: The format of the international meeting The youth dimension The European dimension The needs, issues or aspirations being addressed Why the organisation is proposing the activity How the project differs from previous work Its contribution to Council of Europe youth priorities Objectives and Results Applicants have 3,000 characters to present: The overall aim Specific objectives Expected results Benefits for participants Benefits for communities and organisations Planned outputs and how they will be used Implementation Approach The form provides: 1,800 characters for project phases 1,800 characters for a draft daily programme 1,800 characters for methodological approaches 1,800 characters for the multicultural project team Applicants must explain how the project will incorporate youth participation, inclusion, gender equality and human-rights principles. Partners and Participants The form asks for: Partner names and contact details A description of each partner’s role, limited to 600 characters Participant numbers by country Participant age ranges Participant profiles Recruitment and selection criteria The participant-profile and recruitment section has a limit of 3,600 characters. Applicants can consult the one-off activity narrative application form and one-off activity budget template . Information Required for Long-Term Project Applications The long-term project narrative form asks for: Basic Project Information Contact person Project title Start date End date Complete project duration Proposal Overview Applicants have 3,600 characters to explain: The overall project idea Main activity formats Youth and European dimensions Needs and aspirations being addressed Reasons for proposing the project Connection with the EYF priorities Contribution to the specific objectives of the call Objectives and Results Applicants have 3,000 characters to present: The project aim Main objectives Expected results Benefits for participants and communities Institutional impact Planned outputs and their future use Activities and Methods Applicants have: 1,800 characters for the overview of project activities 1,800 characters for methodological approaches 1,800 characters to describe the multicultural project team Each project activity should have a consistent name and should represent a substantial action that contributes directly to the objectives. Preparatory or evaluation meetings should not be presented as separate activities when they are part of a larger activity. Information for Each Activity For every proposed activity, applicants must provide: Activity name Start and end dates Venue and country Description of what will happen, within 1,800 characters Expected achievements, within 1,200 characters Programme or implementation outline, within 1,800 characters Participant numbers by country Participant age distribution Participant profile and recruitment approach, within 1,800 characters Applicants can consult the long-term project narrative application form and long-term project budget template . Exclusion Criteria for Applicant Organisations An organisation may be excluded where it: Has been convicted of participation in a criminal organisation, corruption, fraud, money laundering, terrorism-related offences, child labour or human trafficking Is bankrupt, insolvent, in liquidation or has ceased operations Has committed serious professional misconduct Has failed to meet tax or social-security obligations Is an empty-shell entity created to avoid legal obligations Has mismanaged Council of Europe or public funds Has an unmanageable conflict of interest Applicants must submit a declaration on honour confirming their compliance. Additional supporting documents may be requested later. Submitting multiple applications for the same proposal is prohibited and may lead to all related applications being excluded. How Applications Will Be Assessed Proposals will be evaluated using the following weighted criteria: Relevance and added value: 40% Quality, clarity and completeness: 32% Cost-effectiveness and completeness of the budget: 16% Expertise and experience of the organisation, partners and project team: 12% The strongest technical proposal cannot compensate for basic ineligibility. Applicants should first confirm organisational, partnership, participant and registration eligibility before investing significant time in drafting. The EYF Secretariat assesses proposals and may request clarifications through the online platform. It then prepares recommendations for the Programming Committee on Youth, which makes the final grant decisions. Indicative Selection and Implementation Timeline 17 August 2026: Calls published 1 October 2026: Application deadline 2 October–15 November 2026: Assessment and dialogue with applicants 14–15 December 2026: Programming Committee on Youth considers and decides on grants 16–18 December 2026: Applicants informed of the results Early January 2027: Grant agreements expected to be signed January–December 2027: One-off activities implemented 1 January–31 March 2027: Long-term projects must begin 30 September 2028: Latest possible completion date for long-term projects Within two months of completion: Final narrative and financial reports due Important Deadline Clarification The announcement, calls webpage and submission sections of the two overview documents state a deadline of 1 October 2026 at 23:59 CET . However, the indicative timetable on the final page of both overview documents labels the same deadline as 23:59 CEST . CET and CEST differ by one hour. Organisations should not rely on the later interpretation. The safest approach is to submit no later than 23:59 CEST on 1 October 2026 , and preferably at least one full working day earlier. Late applications will not be considered except in narrowly defined force-majeure circumstances. Questions and Digital Open Desks Questions must be submitted in English or French no later than one week before the deadline. Questions should be sent to eyf@coe.int , using the relevant subject line: For one-off activities: “Question about EYF call 2027.C5.A” For long-term projects: “Question about EYF call 2027.C6.B” The European Youth Foundation is also organising Digital Open Desk sessions on Microsoft Teams from 14:00 to 16:00 CET on: 19 August 2026 26 August 2026 2 September 2026 9 September 2026 16 September 2026 23 September 2026 30 September 2026 No prior registration is required. Applicants should consult the official announcement for the current Microsoft Teams access link. How to Apply Eligible organisations should follow these steps: Confirm that the organisation is established in a Council of Europe member state. Confirm whether the organisation qualifies for the one-off call, long-term call or both. Create an account on Support4Youth if the organisation does not already have one. Submit the organisation-registration request and all supporting documents. Allow up to two weeks for EYF validation. Read the official call overview, EYF grant guide, narrative form and budget template. Select the relevant Council of Europe youth-sector priority. Build an eligible international partnership and multicultural project team. Design activities involving participants from at least seven Council of Europe member states. Prepare the narrative and financial application in English or French. Explain co-financing and partner contributions clearly. Submit the complete application through Support4Youth before the deadline. Official Application Resources Read the official announcement View all open EYF calls and application documents Access the Support4Youth application platform Read the Guide to EYF Grants Review the Council of Europe Youth Sector Strategy 2030 Read the EYF funding priorities Conclusion The European Youth Foundation Grants 2027 offer substantial support for youth organisations capable of designing credible international projects rooted in democracy, human rights, inclusion, peace and youth participation. The one-off activity call is suitable for organisations planning a focused international youth meeting, with grants available up to €25,000. The long-term project call is designed for eligible international organisations and networks seeking to implement a strategic programme of connected activities over a period of up to 18 months, with funding available up to €60,000. These are demanding institutional grants rather than simple event-sponsorship opportunities. Successful applicants must demonstrate strong alignment with Council of Europe priorities, meaningful youth leadership, international participation, inclusive methods, credible partnerships, sound financial management and clear long-term results. Organisations that are not yet registered should begin immediately because EYF registration can take up to two weeks and must be validated before the application deadline. Complete proposals must be submitted through Support4Youth by 1 October 2026 , with applicants strongly advised to use 23:59 CEST as the safe cutoff and avoid last-minute submission.
