title: Bayreuth Academy International Fellowships 2027–2028 in Germany: 15 Funded Research Residencies for African Studies Scholars Worldwide
summary: Applications are open for the Bayreuth Academy International Fellowships 2027–2028, a funded residential research opportunity offered by the Bayreuth Academy of Advanced African Studies at the University of Bayreuth in Germany. For the 2027–2028 academic year, the Bayreuth Academy will award 15 Individual Fellowships to qualified scholars conducting research in African Studies. The programme brings together researchers from different regions, disciplines and academic career stages to undertake original research, collaborate with University of Bayreuth scholars and contribute to the research agenda of the Africa Multiple Cluster of Excellence. Successful applicants may spend between one and five months at the University of Bayreuth, depending on the selected fellowship term. Support includes a living allowance based on the fellow’s employment status, a monthly mobility allowance, reimbursement of eligible travel expenses, workspace, library access and membership in the Africa Multiple Cluster of Excellence during the fellowship. The application deadline is 5 October 2026 at 23:59 Central European Summer Time, or CEST . Applicants are expected to receive the selection outcome by the end of December 2026. The official fellowship call provides the complete programme details . Bayreuth Academy International Fellowships 2027–2028: Key Details Host institution: Bayreuth Academy of Advanced African Studies University: University of Bayreuth Research organisation: Africa Multiple Cluster of Excellence Location: Bayreuth, Germany Number of fellowships: 15 Individual Fellowships Academic year: 2027–2028 Fellowship format: Mandatory residential research stay Minimum duration: One month Maximum duration: Five months during the winter term or four months during the summer term Minimum qualification: Completed PhD Primary academic field: African Studies Eligible disciplines: Humanities and social, technical and natural sciences Geographical eligibility: Scholars worldwide Application method: Online application Deadline: 5 October 2026 at 23:59 CEST Expected selection notification: By the end of December 2026 Financial support: Living allowance or teaching buyout, travel reimbursement and monthly mobility allowance Special family support: Travel and additional mobility assistance for fellows accompanied by minor children About the Bayreuth Academy of Advanced African Studies The Bayreuth Academy of Advanced African Studies is part of the Africa Multiple Cluster of Excellence at the University of Bayreuth. It serves as an intellectual and institutional platform where international scholars can develop research, exchange ideas and build collaborations around African and African-diasporic societies, experiences and knowledge systems. The Academy’s fellowship programme allows researchers to work within an interdisciplinary community spanning more than 15 academic disciplines. Rather than providing funding for a remote project, the programme is structured as a residential scholarly experience. Fellows are expected to live in Bayreuth during their approved fellowship period and participate actively in the Cluster’s academic community. During the fellowship, successful candidates receive membership status in the Africa Multiple Cluster of Excellence. This gives them the opportunity to connect with researchers, attend scholarly activities and contribute directly to debates concerning the future and reconfiguration of African Studies. About the Africa Multiple Cluster of Excellence The Africa Multiple Cluster of Excellence has been funded through the Excellence Strategy of Germany’s federal and state governments since 1 January 2019. Its central objective is to reconfigure African Studies at both conceptual and structural levels. The Cluster was established as a transformative research environment for studying African and African-diasporic ways of life. It promotes new forms of interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary cooperation while challenging unequal structures in the production, circulation and recognition of knowledge about Africa. The Cluster’s second funding phase, known as Africa Multiple 2.0, covers 2026–2032. Its research focuses on processes of world-making and world-unmaking from the vantage point of Africa. It examines Africa not as an isolated region but as an active participant in the formation of interconnected global worlds. Its research agenda is built around three central concepts: Multiplicity: Recognising that African and African-diasporic realities are heterogeneous, interconnected and continuously changing. Relationality: Examining how institutions, identities, histories, economies, environments and forms of knowledge emerge through relationships. Reflexivity: Encouraging researchers to examine their own positions, methods and the power relations influencing knowledge production. Applicants should read the official Africa Multiple 2.0 research agenda before preparing their proposals. Purpose of the Bayreuth Academy International Fellowship Programme The 15 Individual Fellowships are intended to provide scholars with the time, resources, institutional environment and academic partnerships required to undertake meaningful African Studies research. The programme seeks projects that can make a clear contribution to the Africa Multiple Cluster’s theoretical and thematic priorities. Fellows are expected to pursue academically significant work while engaging with researchers from the University of Bayreuth and the Cluster’s wider international network. The programme is also closely connected to the Cluster’s publication strategy. Applicants should therefore identify credible publication outputs that can result from the proposed fellowship project. The planned research should be capable of producing at least one scholarly publication, preferably for a respected journal or one of the Cluster’s publication outlets. Research Areas and Thematic Sections Applicants may align their projects with one or more of the Cluster’s six Research Sections. These sections function as thematic umbrellas connecting related projects and researchers. 1. Accumulation The Accumulation Research Section examines wealth, ownership, inequality and the processes through which economic and political power are accumulated. Relevant projects may explore land, housing, financial assets, natural resources, labour, inheritance, extractive economic systems and unequal access to wealth and opportunities. The section is particularly concerned with how colonial and postcolonial structures of accumulation continue to shape African societies. 2. Digitalities The Digitalities Research Section investigates digital technologies, artificial intelligence, online platforms, social media, biometrics and digital infrastructures. Research may address data extraction, algorithmic systems, technology-related labour, electronic waste, digital political participation, online communities, cultural expression and the role of technology in social and economic transformation. The section also considers how digital systems may reproduce inequality or contribute to decolonisation and new forms of public participation. 3. Ecologies The Ecologies Research Section focuses on environmental issues, human-environment relationships and the reconfiguration of Environmental Studies in Africa. Relevant topics may include climate change, biodiversity, conservation, Indigenous environmental knowledge, natural-resource governance, environmental justice, colonial and postcolonial environmental structures and African ecological knowledge systems. 4. In/securities The In/securities Research Section considers the interconnected production of security and insecurity. Research may examine political authority, violence, conflict, surveillance, social movements, resource competition, religious organisations, multinational businesses, security agencies, vigilante groups and the ways individuals and communities experience vulnerability, uncertainty and protection. 5. Re The Re Research Section explores memory, heritage and the contested interpretation of the past. Potential areas include monuments, memorials, restitution of cultural objects, museums, colonial legacies, national histories, digital memory, public commemoration and the ways societies remember, challenge, reconstruct or deliberately forget historical events. 6. Translating The Translating Research Section examines translation beyond the narrow transfer of words between languages. It considers how concepts, policies, knowledge, religious ideas, cultural practices and political narratives circulate across multilingual and international settings. Research may also examine artificial intelligence-assisted translation, linguistic power, the dominance of particular languages and the consequences of translating complex ideas across different social contexts. Applicants are not strictly required to place their projects within one of these six Research Sections. Proposals may instead contribute to the Cluster’s broader agenda, particularly its work on world-making, world-unmaking, relationality and the reconfiguration of African Studies. Fellowship Periods and Duration Applicants can propose a residential research stay during either the winter or summer term. Winter Term Fellowship period: Between 1 October 2027 and 29 February 2028 Minimum duration: One month Maximum duration: Five months Summer Term Fellowship period: Between 1 April 2028 and 31 July 2028 Minimum duration: One month Maximum duration: Four months Applicants must indicate their preferred fellowship period in their motivation letter. However, the final start date and duration will depend on the successful applicant’s availability and agreement with the proposed academic host. Physical residence at the University of Bayreuth is compulsory throughout the approved fellowship period. The programme is not offered as a fully remote fellowship. Financial Support and Fellowship Benefits The funding arrangement is divided into three components: Living allowance or teaching buyout Travel reimbursement Monthly mobility allowance The actual living support depends on whether the fellow continues to receive remuneration from a home institution. Case 1: Fellows Without Remuneration From a Home Institution Fellows who do not receive any salary or other remuneration from their home institution may receive: EUR 2,500 per month as a living allowance EUR 750 per month as a mobility allowance Reimbursement of eligible travel expenses to and from Bayreuth The applicant must provide confirmation from their home institution or most recent funding organisation showing that they will not receive remuneration during the fellowship. For an individual fellow without accompanying children, the two listed monthly components amount to EUR 3,250. Travel reimbursement is handled separately. Case 2: Fellows on Paid Leave Without a Replacement Fellows who remain on their home institution’s payroll while taking leave or a sabbatical, but whose institution does not hire a replacement, may receive: EUR 1,000 per month as a living allowance EUR 750 per month as a mobility allowance Reimbursement of eligible travel expenses to and from Bayreuth For an individual fellow in this category, the two listed monthly components amount to EUR 1,750. Case 3: Teaching Buyout Where a fellow continues to receive remuneration from their home institution and a substitute lecturer must be hired, the University of Bayreuth may reimburse the home institution for the replacement lecturer. The teaching-buyout arrangement has an upper limit of: EUR 7,000 per month The official call explains that the teaching-buyout approach may particularly apply to fellowships lasting more than three months. It is not automatically a personal stipend of EUR 7,000 paid directly to the fellow. Instead, the University of Bayreuth agrees with the home institution to reimburse eligible costs associated with employing a substitute lecturer. A formal institutional agreement is not required, but the following evidence must be submitted: A scanned copy of the contract or agreement concerning the substitute lecturer; and Proof that the substitute lecturer’s salary has been paid. The fellow may also receive the applicable mobility allowance and travel reimbursement. Full financial conditions are set out in the official fellowship call and financial provisions . Travel Support The Cluster reimburses eligible travel expenses associated with arrival in and departure from Bayreuth. Reimbursement is made against the submission of receipts. Where a fellow is accompanied by minor children, eligible travel costs may also be reimbursed for the accompanying children. Applicants should retain all relevant tickets, invoices, receipts and proof of payment because the travel support is described as reimbursement rather than a fixed travel grant. Monthly Mobility Allowance All individual fellows are eligible for a monthly mobility allowance of: EUR 750 per month Fellows accompanied by minor children may receive additional monthly mobility support as follows: An additional EUR 250 per month for one accompanying minor child A further EUR 250 per month for a second accompanying minor child A further EUR 250 per month where a third or more minor child or children accompany the fellow The increased mobility allowance is designed to help address the additional costs experienced by scholars travelling with children. Fellows will receive a certificate of payment that must be submitted to the relevant tax authorities. Applicants should therefore check any tax consequences that may apply in Germany or their country of tax residence. Academic and Institutional Benefits In addition to financial assistance, selected fellows receive: Workspace in the new African Studies research building at the University of Bayreuth Access to the University of Bayreuth’s African Studies library holdings Membership in the Africa Multiple Cluster of Excellence during the fellowship Interaction with an international community representing more than 15 academic disciplines Opportunities to collaborate with University of Bayreuth researchers Access to lectures, seminars, discussions and scholarly events Opportunities to present and publish research Participation in academic and social activities Potential engagement with postdoctoral working groups These resources are intended to help fellows complete focused research while becoming active members of the Cluster’s academic environment. Responsibilities of Selected Fellows The Bayreuth Academy fellowship is participatory. Successful applicants are expected to contribute to the academic life of the Academy rather than work in isolation. Fellows are expected to: Participate in Cluster activities: This includes regular Thursday afternoon lectures, seminars and discussion groups held while the fellow is in residence. Deliver a research presentation: Each fellow must give a 45-minute presentation based on their research at the Bayreuth Academy. Engage in scholarly exchange: Fellows should interact informally and formally with Cluster members and other visiting researchers. Collaborate with Bayreuth-based scholars: The proposed fellowship should identify meaningful areas of cooperation with one or more scholars based in Bayreuth. Produce a publication: During or after the fellowship, the fellow is expected to submit at least one publication based on the fellowship project. A high-ranking academic journal or a publication outlet associated with the Cluster is preferred. Record a podcast with the academic host: The podcast discussion should connect the fellow’s project with the Cluster’s themes, concepts, objectives and, where applicable, the selected Research Section. Offer discussion sessions for doctoral students: Fellows should contribute to the intellectual development of doctoral researchers through relevant discussion sessions. Attend social activities: Fellows may be invited to occasional social events organised for the fellowship community. Consider postdoctoral working groups: Participation in one of the Bayreuth Academy’s postdoctoral working groups is optional. Application Requirements Applications must be submitted through the official online form. In addition to general information about the applicant’s academic background, the following materials are required. 1. Complete List of Academic Publications Applicants must upload their full publication list as one PDF file. The list should present the applicant’s research track record clearly and consistently. Because the programme places strong emphasis on publication outcomes, applicants should ensure that publications relevant to African Studies and the proposed project are easy to identify. 2. Curriculum Vitae A complete academic CV must be uploaded as one PDF file. It should include relevant qualifications, appointments, research projects, publications, teaching, grants, awards, conference participation and academic service. 3. Motivation Letter Applicants must provide a motivation letter explaining why they are applying for a Bayreuth Academy fellowship. The letter must: Explain the applicant’s motivation Show how the fellowship supports their research development Demonstrate interest in the Bayreuth Academy and Africa Multiple Cluster State the proposed fellowship period Remain within the maximum limit of 3,500 characters The official instructions indicate that 3,500 characters are approximately equivalent to 500–600 words. 4. Research Project Outline Applicants must submit an outline of the research project they intend to undertake during the fellowship. The project outline must: Explain the research topic and problem Present the project’s objectives and research questions Describe its theoretical or conceptual approach Explain the methodology Show its contribution to African Studies Present a feasible plan for the requested fellowship period Identify the expected outputs, particularly publications The maximum length is 6,500 characters, approximately 1,000–1,100 words. 5. Contribution to the Cluster’s Research Agenda Applicants must provide a separate statement explaining their proposed contribution to the Africa Multiple Cluster’s research agenda or one or more Research Sections. The statement may explain the applicant’s theoretical, methodological or thematic contribution. It must also name the Bayreuth-based scholar or scholars with whom the applicant intends to collaborate. The maximum length is 3,500 characters, approximately 500–600 words. 6. Gender and Diversity Statement Applicants must explain how gender and diversity considerations feature in their proposed research. This should not be treated as a generic equality statement. It should show how gender, social difference, representation, inclusion, research ethics or relevant inequalities are considered within the project’s questions, methods, data, partnerships or anticipated outcomes. The maximum length is 2,000 characters, approximately 300–350 words. 7. Referees Applicants must provide the names and contact details of two referees who can comment on their academic qualifications, research experience and suitability for the programme. How to Apply for the Bayreuth Academy International Fellowships Applicants should follow these steps: Read the fellowship announcement and financial regulations carefully. Study the Africa Multiple 2.0 research agenda and six Research Sections. Confirm that the proposed project has a clear and substantial connection with African Studies. Identify the Research Section or broader Cluster objective that best matches the project. Identify one or more Bayreuth-based scholars with whom meaningful collaboration would be possible. Select a realistic fellowship period within the winter or summer residency window. Prepare the publication list and CV as separate PDF files. Draft the motivation letter, research outline, Cluster-contribution statement and gender-and-diversity statement within their respective character limits. Obtain accurate contact details for two academic referees. Complete the official online application form . Upload all required documents and submit the complete application before the deadline. Applicants should retain a copy of the submitted application and any confirmation generated by the application portal. Important Deadline Clarification The main fellowship announcement and the opening section of the official PDF state that applications close on 5 October 2026 at 23:59 CEST . However, a later applicant-instructions section uses “CET.” Germany will still be observing Central European Summer Time on 5 October 2026 because summer time does not end until the final Sunday of October. Therefore, applicants should treat 23:59 CEST as the safe deadline and submit earlier rather than relying on the one-hour-later CET interpretation. Germany’s official national metrology institute confirms that CEST remains in effect until the last Sunday in October. See the German time-standard guidance . For applicants in Pakistan, 23:59 CEST on 5 October 2026 corresponds to approximately 2:59 a.m. Pakistan Standard Time on 6 October 2026 . Applicants should not wait until this converted local deadline to submit. Expected Selection Timeline Complete applications submitted before the deadline will be considered for the 15 available fellowships. The official instructions state that applicants should be informed of the selection decision by the end of December 2026. Successful applicants will then coordinate the precise fellowship dates and duration with their respective academic hosts. How to Prepare a Competitive Application Based on the published requirements, a strong application should demonstrate the following: A completed PhD and a credible academic publication record A substantial and clearly documented track record in African Studies A focused project that can be advanced meaningfully during a one-to-five-month stay Direct alignment with the Africa Multiple research agenda or one or more Research Sections A clear theoretical, methodological or thematic contribution A realistic and valuable collaboration with named Bayreuth-based scholars A credible publication plan Meaningful integration of gender and diversity considerations A justified choice of fellowship duration and term Evidence that the project can contribute to wider debates on African and African-diasporic worlds Applicants should avoid submitting a generic research proposal that merely mentions Africa. The proposal must demonstrate an informed connection to the Cluster’s goals, concepts and scholarly priorities. Contact for Further Information Questions concerning the fellowship may be directed to: Robert Debusmann Coordinator, Bayreuth Academy of Advanced African Studies Email: robert.debusmann@uni-bayreuth.de Applicants seeking clarification about eligibility, funding status, teaching-buyout arrangements or the deadline terminology should contact the coordinator before submitting. Official Application Links Read the official fellowship announcement Download the official call and financial provisions Read the Africa Multiple research agenda Access the official application form Conclusion The Bayreuth Academy International Fellowships 2027–2028 offer an important opportunity for established African Studies researchers to undertake funded, residential research at the University of Bayreuth in Germany. With 15 fellowships available, the programme supports research across the humanities and social, technical and natural sciences. Its interdisciplinary structure makes it particularly suitable for scholars examining Africa and its diasporas through questions of inequality, digital transformation, ecology, security, memory, language, knowledge and world-making. Beyond financial support, fellows receive access to an international research community, specialist library resources, workspace, academic events and opportunities for collaboration and publication. The programme nevertheless requires serious intellectual engagement: applicants must demonstrate a proven African Studies record, a clearly defined project, alignment with the Cluster’s agenda and a credible plan for collaboration and publication. Qualified applicants should begin preparing their documents early, identify suitable Bayreuth-based collaborators and submit the complete application well before 5 October 2026 at 23:59 CEST . title: Afreximbank–Edordu Research Competition 2026: Postgraduate Research Opportunity for African and Caribbean Scholars
summary: Overview of the Afreximbank–Edordu Research Competition The Afreximbank–Edordu Research Competition is a postgraduate research competition established under the Research Department and Creative and Diaspora Department of the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank) . The competition was conceived in honour of Mr Christopher Edordu , who served as the first President of Afreximbank. The initiative is designed to encourage postgraduate students to engage deeply with some of the most important economic and development questions facing Africa and participating Caribbean states. Through original and rigorous academic research, participants are expected to examine challenges affecting the continent s economic trajectory and develop practical ideas that can contribute to stronger trade, financial systems, regional integration, and sustainable development. The competition provides an avenue for emerging scholars to move beyond theoretical discussions and investigate real-world economic and development issues affecting African and Caribbean economies. It particularly encourages research that can generate meaningful insights, innovative thinking, and actionable solutions. What Is the Afreximbank–Edordu Research Competition? The Afreximbank–Edordu Research Competition is an academic research initiative focused on postgraduate-level research addressing major economic, trade, financial, integration, and sustainable-development issues. The competition seeks to cultivate a new generation of researchers who can critically analyse the challenges confronting Africa and participating Caribbean states while contributing evidence-based ideas for addressing those challenges. Participants are invited to produce rigorous and original research rather than simply summarising existing studies. Their work should demonstrate a strong understanding of the selected issue, critical analysis, and the ability to develop meaningful conclusions or recommendations. The competition s broader objective is to strengthen intellectual engagement with the economic transformation of Africa and its relationships with the Caribbean and the wider global economy. Why the Competition Was Established The competition was conceived in honour of Mr Christopher Edordu , the first President of Afreximbank. His association with the establishment and development of the institution provides an important context for an initiative that encourages research into trade, finance, economic integration, and development. Afreximbank s work is closely connected to the advancement of intra-African trade, economic integration, and sustainable economic development. The research competition complements these broader areas of interest by giving postgraduate scholars an opportunity to investigate critical issues affecting the continent and propose new approaches to existing challenges. By creating a platform for postgraduate research, the initiative also aims to encourage scholars to contribute to discussions that can influence the understanding and future direction of African economic development. Key Research Areas The competition focuses on issues that are central to Africa s economic trajectory. Applicants should therefore consider research questions connected to areas such as: 1. Trade Trade is a major area of focus for the competition. Research may examine challenges and opportunities surrounding African trade, including issues affecting the expansion and strengthening of commercial relationships. Potential research directions could include: African trade and economic transformation Intra-African trade Barriers to trade and market access Trade relationships between Africa and the Caribbean Opportunities for expanding regional and international trade Policies that could strengthen African economies through trade Emerging challenges affecting African participation in global commerce 2. Finance Financial systems play an important role in economic development. Research under the competition may therefore explore issues related to finance and the ability of economies to mobilise and use financial resources effectively. Possible areas of investigation include: Access to finance Financing economic development Financial systems and economic growth Cross-border financial cooperation Innovative approaches to development finance Financial challenges affecting African economies The role of financial institutions in supporting trade and development 3. Economic Integration Economic integration is another central theme. Africa s long-term economic development depends in part on stronger economic relationships between countries and regions. Research could investigate: Regional economic integration African economic cooperation Integration of African markets Cross-border economic activity Policies that can strengthen regional integration Opportunities and challenges associated with deeper economic integration Connections between African and Caribbean economies 4. Sustainable Development The competition also invites research addressing sustainable development. This reflects the need to pursue economic progress while responding to longer-term social, environmental, and economic challenges. Potential research themes could include: Sustainable economic growth Inclusive development Sustainable trade Development financing Economic resilience Long-term development strategies Policies supporting sustainable transformation The relationship between economic development and sustainability What the Competition Is Looking For The competition is not simply about producing an academic paper. It seeks to encourage deep intellectual engagement with the challenges affecting Africa and participating Caribbean states. Successful research should demonstrate several important qualities: Originality: The research should contribute a fresh perspective, argument, finding, or approach. Rigour: The research should be carefully developed and supported by appropriate evidence and analysis. Relevance: The selected issue should relate meaningfully to the economic and development challenges identified by the competition. Critical thinking: Applicants should demonstrate the ability to examine complex problems rather than merely describe them. Practical value: Research should ideally move toward solutions, recommendations, or approaches that could have real-world relevance. Strong academic engagement: Participants should demonstrate meaningful engagement with the relevant research and debates surrounding their chosen subject. Who Can Apply? The competition is intended for postgraduate students across Africa and participating Caribbean states . This means the opportunity is directed toward scholars who are undertaking postgraduate-level studies and whose research can engage with the competition s themes of trade, finance, economic integration, and sustainable development. Eligible applicants should therefore carefully consider whether their postgraduate research and proposed work align with the competition s objectives and subject areas. The description provided for the competition does not specify a particular academic discipline beyond the emphasis on the stated research themes. Consequently, prospective applicants should consult the official competition guidelines for the precise academic, institutional, enrollment, and submission requirements before applying. Learn more about the competition: https://aercafrica.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Afreximbank-Edordu-Research-Competition-Deck.pdf For guide click here https://aercafrica.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/AE-Applicant-Guide-2026.docx.pdf Geographic Eligibility The competition is intended to reach postgraduate researchers from: African countries Participating Caribbean states The available description does not provide a complete list of the Caribbean states participating in the competition. Applicants from the Caribbean should therefore verify whether their country is included in the competition s official definition of participating Caribbean states before preparing a submission. Likewise, the opportunity is presented as being open across Africa rather than being restricted to a particular African subregion or a specific nationality. There is no indication in the provided information that applicants must belong to a particular racial group. The geographic eligibility is instead described in terms of Africa and participating Caribbean states . What Kind of Research Should Applicants Consider? A strong research proposal should identify a meaningful problem connected to the competition s core themes and examine it using a clear research methodology. For example, a postgraduate researcher might investigate: A major barrier preventing greater intra-African trade. How financial innovation could support economic development. Policies that could strengthen regional economic integration. Opportunities for deeper economic cooperation between Africa and the Caribbean. The role of trade in supporting sustainable development. Financial mechanisms capable of supporting sustainable economic transformation. Structural challenges affecting African participation in international markets. Innovative policy solutions for strengthening economic resilience. These examples are illustrative rather than an exhaustive list of approved topics. Applicants should ensure that their actual research question falls within the competition s official requirements. Why This Opportunity Matters for Postgraduate Researchers Postgraduate students frequently conduct research on highly specialised topics, but opportunities to connect academic research directly with major regional economic questions can be limited. The Afreximbank–Edordu Research Competition provides a platform through which postgraduate scholars can direct their academic work toward issues with broader economic and policy significance. The initiative can be particularly valuable for researchers interested in: African economic development International trade Regional integration Development finance Economic policy Sustainable development Africa–Caribbean relations Financial systems International economic cooperation By encouraging original research and actionable solutions, the competition creates an opportunity for postgraduate researchers to contribute to conversations that extend beyond the university environment. How Applicants Can Prepare Although applicants should follow the official competition rules and submission requirements, prospective participants can strengthen their preparation by taking several steps. 1. Select a Clearly Defined Research Problem Avoid choosing an overly broad topic. A well-defined research question allows the researcher to conduct deeper analysis and develop more convincing conclusions. 2. Connect the Topic to the Competition s Themes The research should have a clear relationship with one or more of the competition s central areas: Trade Finance Economic integration Sustainable development 3. Conduct Thorough Research Applicants should review relevant academic literature, policy documents, economic data, and other credible sources that can support their analysis. 4. Develop an Original Argument The competition emphasises original research. Applicants should therefore identify what their work adds to existing discussions. 5. Focus on Actionable Solutions Where appropriate, researchers should move beyond identifying problems and consider realistic solutions, policy options, or recommendations. 6. Review the Official Requirements Applicants should carefully verify the official competition guidelines, including eligibility requirements, research specifications, formatting instructions, submission procedures, deadlines, and any other conditions. Deadline No application deadline is provided in the information supplied for this opportunity. Prospective applicants should check the official Afreximbank–Edordu Research Competition announcement or competition guidelines for the current submission deadline before beginning or finalising their application. More details HERE Important Details at a Glance Detail Information Opportunity Afreximbank–Edordu Research Competition Organising departments Afreximbank Research Department and Creative and Diaspora Department Honours Mr Christopher Edordu, Afreximbank s first President Target participants Postgraduate students Geographic focus Africa and participating Caribbean states Main themes Trade, finance, economic integration, and sustainable development Research requirement Rigorous and original research Focus Critical engagement with economic and development challenges Expected contribution Innovative and actionable solutions Deadline Not provided in the supplied information Conclusion The Afreximbank–Edordu Research Competition offers postgraduate students an opportunity to place their academic research within some of the most important economic and development conversations affecting Africa and participating Caribbean states. By focusing on trade, finance, economic integration, and sustainable development , the competition encourages scholars to investigate complex challenges, think critically about the continent s economic trajectory, and develop innovative solutions with practical relevance. For postgraduate researchers whose academic interests intersect with African economic development, international trade, finance, regional integration, sustainability, or Africa–Caribbean economic relations, this competition represents an opportunity to turn rigorous academic research into a contribution to wider policy and development discussions. Interested postgraduate students should carefully review the official competition guidelines to confirm their eligibility, identify the applicable requirements, verify the participating Caribbean states, and confirm the submission deadline before applying. title: UNFPA Foresight Paid Intern 2026: Strategic Foresight and Futures Work Internship in Nairobi, Kenya (Remote)
summary: The United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) is offering an exciting opportunity for students and recent graduates interested in strategic foresight, futures thinking, international development, public policy, data analysis, demographic change, and strategic planning through its Foresight and Futures Work Internship . The internship is based within the Strategic Planning Branch of the UNFPA Programme Division and will provide the successful intern with practical exposure to how strategic foresight is applied within a United Nations development organization. The role will involve research, trend analysis, horizon scanning, scenario thinking, knowledge management, training support, stakeholder engagement, and the use of AI-assisted tools for foresight analysis. The position is listed as Nairobi, Kenya (Remote) and is expected to begin in September 2026 for an initial period of three months, with the possibility of extension. For students and recent graduates seeking international experience and practical exposure to strategic planning and anticipatory governance, this internship offers an opportunity to work alongside professionals across UNFPA Headquarters, Regional Offices, Country Offices, United Nations Country Teams, and other development partners. UNFPA has identified strategic foresight as a corporate priority under its Strategic Plan 2026–2029 . The organization is using foresight approaches to strengthen anticipatory governance, adaptive programming, and long-term decision-making. The Foresight and Futures Work Intern will support efforts to make foresight a more established part of UNFPA s work. This includes helping Country Offices and United Nations Country Teams explore future trends, identify emerging signals, understand potential changes, and use forward-looking analysis when developing programmes and strategies. The internship therefore goes beyond traditional administrative work. The successful candidate will have opportunities to contribute to analytical and knowledge-based activities related to the future of development, demographic change, strategic planning, and organizational transformation. Why Strategic Foresight Matters at UNFPA The global development environment is increasingly complex and uncertain. Organizations need to understand not only what is happening today, but also what emerging trends and potential disruptions could affect their programmes and priorities in the future. UNFPA is responding to this need by expanding the use of Futures Trend Analysis (FTA) and other strategic foresight methodologies. These approaches can help inform: Country Programme Documents (CPDs) Strategic planning processes Policy development Adaptive programming Organizational transformation United Nations Country Team initiatives Long-term development planning Anticipatory governance Organizational learning and innovation UNFPA Headquarters is supporting a growing number of Country Offices and United Nations Country Teams in conducting Futures Trend Analysis and other foresight exercises. The increasing demand for technical support, analytical products, training, knowledge management, and practical tools has created the need for additional support in expanding this work. The internship is positioned within this growing area of work. The Role of Artificial Intelligence in the Internship An important aspect of this internship is exposure to AI-assisted foresight methods . UNFPA is using internally developed AI-assisted tools to support activities such as: Horizon scanning Signal classification Signal clustering Trend analysis Foresight research However, the use of AI does not replace human analysis. The tools are applied under human review at every stage of analysis . The intern may therefore gain practical experience in evaluating and supporting AI-assisted foresight processes, including prompt design, classification, testing, documentation, and human-in-the-loop verification. This makes the opportunity particularly relevant for candidates interested in the intersection of artificial intelligence, data analysis, strategic planning, and international development . Main Responsibilities of the UNFPA Foresight Intern The selected intern will support the implementation of UNFPA s corporate strategic foresight agenda through a range of research, analytical, coordination, training, and knowledge-management activities. 1. Support Futures Trend Analysis Exercises The intern will assist with the design and implementation of Futures Trend Analysis (FTA) exercises for selected UNFPA Country Offices. These exercises are intended to help Country Offices better understand emerging trends and potential future developments and use that information to strengthen: Country Programme Documents Strategic planning Adaptive programming Future-oriented decision-making This responsibility can provide valuable experience in applying futures methodologies to real-world international development challenges. 2. Support UN Country Team Foresight Exercises The intern will also support the design, coordination, and facilitation of strategic foresight exercises conducted by UNFPA-led United Nations Country Teams (UNCTs) . This work may involve collaboration with: Resident Coordinators Offices UN agencies Development partners UNFPA Country Offices Other stakeholders involved in development planning The role can therefore provide exposure to the collaborative nature of strategic planning within the United Nations system. 3. Contribute to Foresight Training Programmes The intern will support the delivery of strategic foresight training programmes for UNFPA staff at different organizational levels. These may include personnel working at: UNFPA Headquarters Regional Offices Country Offices Responsibilities may include preparing: Training materials Practical exercises Participant resources Learning materials Presentation content This component can help the intern develop both technical knowledge and communication skills. 4. Support Webinars, Workshops and Communities of Practice The intern will assist in planning and delivering global knowledge-sharing activities, including: Webinars Workshops Communities of Practice Other learning and knowledge-sharing events These activities are designed to strengthen foresight capabilities across the organization and encourage the exchange of experiences and good practices. 5. Develop Foresight Guidance and Knowledge Products Another important responsibility will be supporting the development and continuous improvement of practical resources that help institutionalize foresight across UNFPA. These resources may include: Foresight guidance Learning materials Toolkits Training modules Knowledge products Practical tools The work will help make foresight methodologies more accessible and usable across different parts of the organization. 6. Support Knowledge Management The intern will contribute to documenting and organizing knowledge generated through foresight initiatives. This may involve documenting: Lessons learned Case studies Good practices Analytical outputs Emerging practices Experiences from different countries The objective is to promote organizational learning and facilitate collaboration and knowledge sharing across countries and offices. 7. Support AI-Assisted Foresight Tools The intern will also support the application and continued development of AI-assisted foresight tools. This may include helping with: Developing evaluation criteria Creating test cases Testing tools Documenting tool performance Supporting iterative improvement Prompt design Signal classification Human-in-the-loop verification Candidates interested in AI, research, data analysis, and emerging technologies may find this particularly valuable. Qualifications and Eligibility Requirements The opportunity is aimed at students and recent graduates with an academic background relevant to strategic foresight, development, policy, social sciences, economics, data, or related areas. Applicants should meet the following academic requirement: Hold a Bachelor s or Master s degree , while being either enrolled in the final year of study or having graduated within the past 12 months . The degree should be in Futures Studies, International Development, Public Policy, Political Science, Economics, Sociology, Demography, Development Studies, Data Science, International Relations, or another relevant discipline . Beyond academic qualifications, applicants should demonstrate an interest in areas such as: Strategic foresight Futures thinking Scenario planning Systems thinking Strategic planning Skills and Experience Desired Successful candidates are expected to have strong analytical and communication abilities. Relevant skills include: Research and Analysis Applicants should have strong: Research skills Analytical skills Writing skills Information synthesis abilities Experience conducting literature reviews and synthesizing complex information is particularly relevant. Research Methods and Data Familiarity with: Qualitative research methods Data analysis is desirable. Candidates with experience interpreting complex information and turning research findings into clear analytical outputs may therefore be well suited to the position. Communication The role requires excellent: Communication skills Presentation skills Collaboration skills Because the intern may contribute to training sessions, webinars, workshops, and knowledge-sharing activities, the ability to communicate complex concepts clearly is important. Organizational Skills Applicants should demonstrate: Strong organizational skills Attention to detail Ability to manage tasks responsibly Ability to work independently Ability to collaborate effectively Technology Skills Applicants should be proficient in Microsoft Office applications . Additional experience with the following would be an advantage: AI tools Visualization tools Collaboration tools Language Requirements Fluency in English is required. Knowledge of another United Nations language is considered an asset. Candidates who can work effectively in multicultural and multilingual environments may therefore have an additional advantage. What the Intern Can Learn The internship is designed not only as a work placement but also as a learning opportunity. By the end of the internship, the intern should have developed a stronger understanding of UNFPA and its Strategic Plan 2026–2029 and gained practical experience in applying strategic foresight within an international development organization. Strategic Foresight Experience The intern can gain practical exposure to: Horizon scanning Trend analysis Weak signal identification Scenario development Futures methodologies Strategic foresight processes This experience can be particularly useful for students and recent graduates considering careers in strategic planning, policy analysis, futures studies, international development, or organizational transformation. Understanding Demographic Change Because of UNFPA s mandate, the internship also provides an opportunity to better understand demographic change and its implications for sustainable development . This can help candidates connect population trends and demographic developments with broader questions of development planning and policy. United Nations Experience The intern will gain exposure to United Nations Country Team foresight exercises and strategic planning processes. Working across Headquarters, Regional Offices, Country Offices, and UN partners can provide insight into how large international organizations coordinate strategic initiatives across different levels. Adaptive Management and Country Programming The intern is expected to develop greater knowledge of how foresight can be integrated into: Country programme design Strategic planning Adaptive management Development programming This is particularly relevant for individuals interested in international development and public policy. Facilitation and Communication Participation in workshops, webinars, training activities, and Communities of Practice can help strengthen: Facilitation skills Presentation skills Communication skills Stakeholder engagement skills Multicultural Teamwork The internship will involve collaboration in a multicultural and multidisciplinary environment spanning headquarters, regional, and country offices. This can help interns develop professional experience working with people from different backgrounds, disciplines, locations, and areas of expertise. Innovation and Anticipatory Governance The intern will also develop an improved understanding of: Innovation Anticipatory governance Organizational learning Strategic foresight within the UN system These are increasingly relevant areas for organizations seeking to prepare for uncertainty and emerging challenges. AI-Assisted Foresight A particularly modern learning component is practical exposure to AI-assisted foresight methods. The amount of the stipend varies according to factors including: Duty station Internship modality Applicants should therefore understand that the internship is not a salaried employment position and should consider their financial arrangements before accepting the placement. title: Research Fellow (Cadbury Postdoctoral Fellowship) in African Studies at the University of Birmingham, UK – 2027.
summary: The University of Birmingham is inviting applications for the Research Fellow (Cadbury Postdoctoral Fellowship) in African Studies , an academic opportunity designed to support an early-career researcher whose work focuses on African History and/or African Studies . Based in the University s School of History and Cultures in Edgbaston, Birmingham, the fellowship provides an opportunity for an eligible scholar to undertake advanced research, publish academic work, contribute to teaching, and participate in the University s wider research community. The position is particularly significant because it is funded through an endowment established to enable academics from sub-Saharan African universities to spend a period of time at the University of Birmingham. Importantly, this is not an open international postdoctoral fellowship . Applicants must currently be based on the African continent and employed by or affiliated with an African higher education institution . Research Fellow (Cadbury Postdoctoral Fellowship) in African Studies The successful candidate will join the School of History and Cultures at the University of Birmingham as a Research Fellow in African History. The fellowship is intended to strengthen the candidate s research profile while also contributing to the University s teaching and research activities in African Studies and History. The role will involve working with a mentor on an agreed programme of research and developing research outputs suitable for publication and academic dissemination. Key opportunity details Institution: University of Birmingham School: School of History and Cultures Location: Edgbaston, Birmingham, United Kingdom Position: Research Fellow (Cadbury Postdoctoral Fellowship) in African Studies Field: African History and/or African Studies Contract: Full-time, fixed-term Contract period: Up to June 2028 Fellowship duration: 18 months Expected start date: 1 January 2027 Salary: £36,636–£46,049 per year, with potential progression to £48,822 Grade: Grade 7 Application deadline: 1 September 2026 Job identification: 9655 About the Cadbury Postdoctoral Fellowship The Cadbury Postdoctoral Fellowship is intended to create an opportunity for scholars affiliated with higher education institutions in sub-Saharan Africa to spend a period of research at the University of Birmingham. During the fellowship, the successful researcher will be able to develop their academic work in an international research environment while contributing to the teaching and intellectual life of the University. The fellow will work within the School of History and Cultures and will have the opportunity to engage with researchers and students working in related fields. The fellowship is therefore particularly relevant to researchers who have already completed a PhD in African History or a closely related field and are looking to strengthen their postdoctoral research and publication record. What will the Research Fellow do? The successful candidate will have responsibilities across research, publication, teaching, academic engagement and administration. 1. Conduct high-quality research A central component of the position will be developing and undertaking research within the fellow s area of historical specialisation. The fellow will: Develop research objectives and proposals. Conduct research within their area of expertise. Collect and analyse research data. Interpret research findings. Develop new intellectual understandings through their research. Work with a mentor where appropriate. Address challenges that may affect research objectives and deadlines. Research methods may include literature reviews, interviews, archival or other research approaches appropriate to the field. 2. Develop academic publications The position places significant emphasis on research outputs and academic publications. The successful candidate will be expected to: Disseminate research findings. Prepare academic publications. Present research at seminars and other academic events. Prepare papers, posters and other research outputs. Contribute to the University s research environment. Develop a convincing and achievable research and publication programme. Applicants therefore need to demonstrate research activity and publications appropriate to their stage of their postdoctoral career. APPLY HERE. 3. Contribute to teaching The Research Fellow will also contribute to the delivery of African Studies and History programmes within the School of History and Cultures. Teaching responsibilities may include: Designing and delivering teaching sessions. Convening undergraduate or postgraduate modules. Delivering lectures. Conducting seminars. Designing and marking assessments. Supervising dissertation students where appropriate. Supporting other teaching-related activities. Candidates should therefore be able to contribute to teaching at both undergraduate and Master s level in African Studies and History. 4. Participate in the University s research community The successful fellow will contribute to research-related activities within the Department, School and wider University. This can include: Participating in research seminars. Presenting research findings. Engaging with academic colleagues. Supporting research-related activities. Participating in public engagement activities. Contributing to wider scholarly discussions. The role therefore goes beyond independent research and encourages the successful candidate to become an active member of the University s academic community. 5. Support students and other researchers Depending on the requirements of the discipline and research activities, the fellow may also: Supervise students undertaking research-related work. Provide guidance to PhD students. Support staff or students assisting with research. Offer academic guidance within their area of expertise. 6. Research administration and management The position may also involve administrative responsibilities arising from the research programme. The successful candidate may contribute to: Research-related administration. Departmental activities. School-level research activities. Management processes. Public engagement activities. Equality, diversity and inclusion initiatives. Who can apply? This fellowship has specific eligibility requirements , particularly concerning the applicant s location, institutional affiliation and doctoral qualification. PhD requirement Applicants must have a PhD focused on the history of Africa and/or African diasporas . The PhD must have been: Examined and passed between 1 June 2021 and 1 June 2026 . Applicants whose doctoral thesis has only been submitted and is awaiting examination are not eligible . This means candidates must have successfully completed the examination process within the specified period before applying. African continent requirement Applicants must currently be based on the African continent . In addition, they must be: Employed by an African higher education institution; or Affiliated with an African higher education institution. This is one of the most important eligibility conditions of the opportunity. The fellowship is specifically funded to enable members of staff at sub-Saharan African universities to spend a period at the University of Birmingham. Therefore, applicants living outside Africa are not eligible simply because they are originally from an African country. The requirement concerns the applicant s current location and institutional affiliation . Employment status requirement Candidates must either: Not currently hold a permanent academic position , or If they do hold a permanent academic position, provide a statement with their application confirming that their home institution will release them for the duration of their appointment at the University of Birmingham. Applicants should therefore carefully consider their employment status before applying. Other skills and experience required Successful applicants should be able to demonstrate: Research experience Applicants should have evidence of: Active research engagement. Academic publications. Research outputs appropriate to their career stage. Ability to develop independent research. Ability to analyse and interpret research findings. Research proposal development Candidates need to demonstrate the ability to develop a convincing and achievable research and publication proposal in African History . The proposed research should be realistic for the fellowship period and demonstrate clear academic value. Teaching experience Applicants should be capable of contributing to: Undergraduate teaching. Master s-level teaching. African Studies programmes. History programmes. Administrative and organisational skills The position also requires an understanding of broader academic management and administrative processes. Salary and employment conditions The position is a full-time, fixed-term Grade 7 appointment . The stated salary range is: £36,636 to £46,049 per year , with potential progression once in post to £48,822 . The expected start date is 1 January 2027 , and the contract is scheduled to run on a fixed-term basis up to June 2028 . The fellowship itself is described as an 18-month postdoctoral fellowship . Application deadline The stated closing date is: 1 September 2026 Applicants should ensure that they submit their application before the deadline and allow enough time to prepare their research and publication proposal and demonstrate their eligibility. Important eligibility point for African scholars One of the most important aspects of this opportunity is that it is not simply a fellowship for anyone interested in African Studies . The position specifically states that it is limited to applicants who are: Currently based on the African continent ; and Employed by or affiliated with an African higher education institution . Applicants must also have a qualifying PhD in the history of Africa and/or African diasporas, completed within the specified period. Consequently, researchers from African countries who are currently living and working outside Africa may not satisfy the eligibility requirements. Similarly, an applicant who is currently living in Africa but has no employment or affiliation with an African higher education institution would need to carefully assess whether they meet the stated institutional requirement. CLICK HERE for more information. Application considerations Candidates should ensure that their application clearly demonstrates how they meet the requirements of the fellowship. A strong application should make it easy for the University to identify: The applicant s doctoral qualification. The date on which the PhD was examined and passed. Their current location on the African continent. Their affiliation with an African higher education institution. Their research specialisation. Their publication record. Their proposed research programme. Their ability to contribute to African Studies and History teaching. Their ability to participate in the wider academic environment. Their ability to complete an achievable research and publication programme during the fellowship. Use of AI in applications The University of Birmingham specifically provides a warning regarding the use of artificial intelligence in applications. Applicants are expected to demonstrate their genuine interest in the role and ensure that written application materials accurately reflect their own communication style. The University states that applications relying too heavily on AI tools may appear generic and may not provide enough detail for the University to properly assess the applicant s skills. Applicants should therefore ensure that their application materials are genuinely their own and accurately represent their research experience, academic interests and professional background. Equality, diversity and inclusion The University of Birmingham states that it values diversity and is committed to creating an inclusive working environment. The University highlights its work through initiatives and accreditations including: Athena SWAN. Race Equality Charter. Disability Confident accreditation. Equality, Diversity and Inclusion Centre. The successful candidate will be expected to contribute to a fair and equitable workplace and to identify and respond appropriately to equality and diversity issues in accordance with University policies. Informal enquiries Applicants who have questions about the position can make informal enquiries to: Juliet Gilbert Email: j.gilbert.2@bham.ac.uk Why this opportunity is significant The Cadbury Postdoctoral Fellowship provides an opportunity for an eligible African scholar to spend an extended period conducting research at a major UK university while remaining connected to their academic development and research interests. For an early-career researcher in African History or African Studies, the position can provide an environment for: Developing new research. Strengthening academic publications. Building international academic connections. Participating in seminars and research activities. Gaining additional teaching experience. Engaging with scholars and students in the UK. Developing a longer-term academic profile. Contributing research on Africa and African diasporas to an international academic environment. Opportunity Category Fellowship — Postdoctoral Research Fellowship Who Qualifies? This opportunity is specifically aimed at early-career African scholars/researchers who: Have a PhD in the history of Africa and/or African diasporas . Had their PhD examined and passed between 1 June 2021 and 1 June 2026 . Are currently based on the African continent . Are employed by or affiliated with an African higher education institution . Have evidence of research activity and publications. Can develop a convincing research and publication proposal in African History. Can contribute to undergraduate and Master s teaching in African Studies and History. The opportunity is therefore Africa-focused rather than open to applicants from every continent . The current location and African higher education affiliation requirements are particularly important.
