title: Getty Conservation Guest Scholars Program 2026: Fully Funded Three-Month Research Opportunity for Cultural Heritage Conservation Professionals.
summary: Professionals and established researchers working in cultural heritage conservation and preservation have an opportunity to undertake advanced independent research through the Getty Conservation Guest Scholars Program 2026 . Organized by the Getty Conservation Institute (GCI) , the program provides selected scholars with a three-month residency at the Getty in Los Angeles, California. The residency is designed to give experienced conservation professionals dedicated time and access to specialist resources to develop research projects that can contribute new knowledge, methods, and perspectives to the conservation field. The program is particularly valuable for professionals whose research can benefit from the Getty s research collections, library resources, intellectual community, and conservation expertise. Applications are currently open, and interested applicants must submit their materials by October 1, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. Los Angeles time (GMT-7) . About the Getty Conservation Guest Scholars Program The Conservation Guest Scholars Program provides an opportunity for established scholars and professionals who have achieved distinction in the field of cultural heritage conservation to spend three months in residence at the Getty Conservation Institute. During the residency, scholars are able to pursue their own research projects without their usual work-related obligations. This dedicated research period allows participants to concentrate on projects that could advance professional practice and contribute to wider discussions within cultural heritage conservation. Scholars also become part of the intellectual community at Getty. During their residency, they can interact with other Getty scholars, fellows, interns, and professionals while making use of resources available at the Getty Center and Getty Villa. The program has been active since 2000 and remains an important opportunity for professionals seeking to undertake independent research related to the conservation and preservation of cultural heritage. What Is the Main Goal of the Program? The central goal of the Conservation Guest Scholars Program is to support research that brings new knowledge and fresh perspectives to cultural heritage conservation . Getty is interested in projects that can make meaningful contributions to conservation practice. Research may address areas involving cultural heritage objects, collections, architecture, sites, or related conservation and preservation challenges. Successful applicants are expected to use their residency productively and independently, developing research that has clear relevance to the broader conservation field. What Does the Three-Month Residency Offer? Selected Conservation Guest Scholars spend three months in residence at the Getty Conservation Institute. The available residency periods are: September–December January–March April–June The grant provides $21,500 for the three-month residency. In addition to the financial grant, selected scholars receive several forms of practical and research support. Key benefits include: A $21,500 grant for the three-month residency. A workstation at the Conservation Institute . An apartment in the Getty scholar housing complex . Research assistance . A travel stipend . An available healthcare option . Access to Getty research resources and collections. Opportunities to engage with Getty scholars, fellows, interns, and other members of the intellectual community. Dedicated time to pursue an independent research project without normal work-related obligations. The terms stated above apply as of August 2026 and may be subject to future changes. Who Can Apply for the Getty Conservation Guest Scholars Program? The program welcomes applications from researchers and practitioners working in cultural heritage conservation or preservation . Eligible areas can include work involving: Cultural heritage objects. Museum and heritage collections. Architecture. Historic and cultural sites. Conservation practice. Preservation. Related areas of cultural heritage research. Applicants must have significant professional experience and an established record demonstrating their contribution to the field. For more information CLICK HERE. Professional Experience Requirement Applicants should have at least seven years of professional experience . They should also have an established record of: Publications. Professional contributions. Research. Conservation practice. Other achievements demonstrating distinction in the field. Getty particularly encourages individuals from groups that are underrepresented within the cultural heritage conservation field to apply. Important Academic Restrictions The Conservation Guest Scholars Program is intended for established professionals and researchers rather than applicants pursuing initial doctoral-level research. The program does not consider proposals for postdoctoral research or research that contributes toward a PhD or another academic degree . Recent PhD graduates in chemistry and other physical or material sciences are instead directed toward Getty s Postdoctoral Fellowship in Conservation Science , which is a separate opportunity. Applicants should therefore make sure their proposed project fits the purpose of the Conservation Guest Scholars Program before applying. APPLY HERE. Can Applicants Use Getty s Science Laboratories? The Getty Conservation Institute may consider proposals that require access to its science laboratories. However, laboratory use is dependent on: The availability of appropriate laboratory facilities. Staff availability. The amount of available staff time. Laboratory access therefore cannot be guaranteed . Applicants whose projects involve Getty s scientific facilities should also be prepared to conduct their research independently rather than relying on Getty Science department staff to carry out the work. This is an important consideration when designing the proposed research methodology. Eligibility for Previous Grant Recipients Previous recipients of a Conservation Guest Scholar Grant may apply again, but they must observe a six-year waiting period before reapplying. This means previous participation does not permanently prevent someone from applying again, provided the required waiting period has been completed. Who Cannot Apply? Certain individuals are excluded from the program. The following are not eligible: Current Getty staff members. Members of the immediate families of current Getty staff members. Applicants proposing postdoctoral research. Applicants proposing research that contributes toward a PhD or another academic degree. Applicants should carefully review these restrictions before investing time in preparing an application. What Kind of Research Project Is Getty Looking For? The quality and relevance of the proposed research project are central to the selection process. A strong proposal should demonstrate an original research topic , a clearly defined methodology, realistic outcomes, and a meaningful contribution to conservation practice. Applicants should explain not only what they want to research but also why the project matters to the wider field. A strong project should clearly address: What is the research problem? Why is the topic important to cultural heritage conservation? What methodology will be used? What part of the research will be conducted during the Getty residency? What outcomes are expected? How could the project advance conservation practice? Why is the applicant qualified to undertake the research? Why are Getty s resources particularly valuable to the project? The strongest applications will make a convincing case that Getty is an appropriate and necessary environment for the proposed research. Application Requirements Applicants are required to submit several important components through the Getty Foundation Grant Portal. 1. Project Proposal The project proposal must not exceed five typed, double-spaced pages . The proposal must include distinct sections covering: Project description Methodology , including which components will be pursued while the applicant is in residence at Getty Expected outcome Contribution of the project to advancing practice in the conservation field Applicant s qualifications to execute the project Benefits of Getty resources to the project Applicants should ensure that the proposal remains focused and clearly connects their research goals with the resources and intellectual environment available at Getty. 2. Abridged Curriculum Vitae Applicants must provide an abridged CV highlighting their most relevant professional activities. The CV must not exceed five typed, single-spaced pages . Rather than submitting an unnecessarily long professional history, applicants should prioritize experience, research, publications, conservation work, and achievements that demonstrate their ability to successfully complete the proposed project. 3. Selected Bibliography Applicants must also submit a selected bibliography. This section should identify scholarly works, other than the applicant s own publications, that are important to the proposed research and help establish the project s intellectual framework. The selected bibliography must not exceed two typed, single-spaced pages . Applicants should select sources that demonstrate their understanding of the existing scholarship surrounding their research topic. How Applications Are Submitted Applications are submitted through the Getty Foundation Grant Portal . When applications are open, applicants can: Create an account. Update their account information. Create a new application. Save their application. Return later to continue working on the application. Getty recommends using Google Chrome for the best experience with the application portal. Applicants may also use Firefox or Safari . Internet Explorer is not compatible with the portal. Applicants should also be careful when returning to a saved application. After creating and saving an application form, applicants should return through the Applications: In Progress section of the portal. Creating a new application instead of returning to the saved version could result in accidentally creating multiple versions of the same application. Getty Conservation Guest Scholar Application Deadline The deadline for submitting application materials is: October 1, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. Los Angeles time (GMT-7). Applicants should not wait until the final hours to submit their applications. Preparing a strong research proposal, CV, bibliography, and supporting materials can take considerable time. It is advisable to begin preparation well before the deadline and allow sufficient time to review all application materials before submission. How Will Applications Be Evaluated? The Conservation Guest Scholar Grants are awarded through a competitive selection process. Applications are evaluated according to several major criteria. Overall Quality of the Application Reviewers consider the strength, clarity, coherence, and overall quality of the submitted application. Applicants should ensure that all parts of the application work together and clearly communicate the purpose and value of the proposed research. Contribution to Conservation Practice The proposed research should have the potential to contribute to the advancement of practice within the cultural heritage conservation field. Applicants should clearly explain the potential significance of their research beyond their own professional or academic interests. Applicant s Past Achievements Getty considers the applicant s previous accomplishments and professional record. A strong history of relevant professional work, publications, research, and other contributions can demonstrate the applicant s capacity to complete the proposed project. Qualifications to Undertake the Project Applicants must demonstrate that they possess the experience, knowledge, and professional expertise required to successfully execute their research. The proposed project should be realistic in relation to the applicant s background and capabilities. Benefit of Getty Resources Applicants must clearly explain how the project would benefit from Getty s resources. This may include: Getty library collections. Research collections. Conservation resources. Getty s intellectual community. Relevant staff expertise. Other resources available through the Getty Center and Getty Villa. A strong application should avoid simply stating that Getty is prestigious. Instead, applicants should identify specific resources and explain how those resources will directly support their research. Letters of Reference Are Not Considered Applicants should note that letters of reference are not considered in the application evaluation . Therefore, applicants should focus their preparation on the required application materials and on developing a strong, clearly structured research proposal. How Does the Selection Process Work? Applications go through a rigorous screening process involving two separate selection committees . The committees include: Current Getty staff members. External experts with backgrounds in conservation. Experts from adjacent fields of study outside Getty. This multidisciplinary review process allows applications to be assessed from both conservation-specific and broader professional perspectives. What Makes a Strong Application? According to the program s evaluation approach, strong applications should demonstrate several important qualities. Originality The proposed research should address an original or meaningful topic capable of adding new knowledge or perspectives to conservation. Clear Methodology Applicants should explain exactly how they intend to conduct the research and what activities will be undertaken during the residency. Defined Outcomes The proposal should identify realistic and meaningful outcomes that could emerge from the research. Impact on the Field Applicants should explain how their project could contribute to conservation practice and why the findings could matter to other professionals. Independent Research Capacity Applicants should demonstrate that they can work independently, particularly because access to Getty staff expertise and laboratory facilities cannot always be guaranteed. Strong Case for Getty One of the most important elements is explaining why Getty is the right place to undertake the proposed research. Applicants should connect their project directly to Getty s collections, library, facilities, research environment, or other available resources. When Will Applicants Receive a Decision? Applicants are expected to be notified of the Getty Conservation Institute s decision by March or April 2027 . This means applicants should be prepared for a selection process that continues for several months after the October 2026 application deadline. Relationship With Other Getty Scholar Programs The Conservation Guest Scholars Program is related to other Getty residential research opportunities, including the Getty Scholars Program at the Villa . The Getty Villa Scholars Program supports advanced research that contributes to understanding and preserving cultural heritage, particularly in relation to the arts and cultures of antiquity. Conservation Guest Scholars and Getty Villa Scholars live within the same complex and participate in shared activities and lectures. This creates opportunities for intellectual exchange and collaboration between researchers working in related areas. However, applicants should note that the programs have separate application processes . Applying to one does not constitute an application to the other. Frequently Asked Questions and Further Information Getty provides a collection of frequently asked questions addressing common issues concerning its residential grant opportunities. Applicants who still have questions about the Conservation Guest Scholars Program can contact the Getty Conservation Institute at: gcischolars@getty.edu Applicants should use the official Getty information and application portal when preparing and submitting their applications. Why This Opportunity Is Significant The Getty Conservation Guest Scholars Program can be particularly valuable for experienced cultural heritage professionals who have a research project but lack the dedicated time, facilities, collections, or intellectual environment needed to develop it fully. The three-month residency creates an opportunity to step away from normal professional obligations and concentrate on an independent research project. The combination of financial support, housing, travel assistance, research resources, and access to the Getty s scholarly community makes the program a substantial professional development opportunity. For professionals working across conservation, museums, heritage sites, architecture, collections, and related areas, the program can provide an environment for developing research with potential implications for the wider field. Tips for Preparing a Competitive Application Applicants interested in applying can strengthen their submissions by taking a strategic approach. 1. Start With a Focused Research Question Avoid making the project unnecessarily broad. Clearly identify the problem or question the research intends to address. 2. Explain the Conservation Relevance Make a direct connection between the research and cultural heritage conservation practice. 3. Make the Getty Connection Specific Do not simply state that Getty has excellent resources. Identify the particular collections, library resources, facilities, or research environment that will help the project. 4. Demonstrate Independence Since the research is expected to be independently conducted, applicants should show that they have the expertise and capacity to execute the project. 5. Keep the Proposal Within the Page Limit The project proposal must not exceed five typed, double-spaced pages. Applicants should therefore prioritize the most important information. 6. Present Relevant Professional Experience The abridged CV should focus on achievements that demonstrate the applicant s ability to undertake the proposed research. 7. Develop a Strong Intellectual Framework The selected bibliography should show that the applicant understands important existing scholarship related to the proposed project. 8. Apply Early Because the deadline is based on Los Angeles time, applicants in other parts of the world should take the time difference into account and submit before the final deadline. Key Details at a Glance Program: Getty Conservation Guest Scholars Program Organizer: Getty Conservation Institute Location: Getty, Los Angeles, California Residency: Three months Grant: $21,500 Housing: Apartment in Getty scholar housing complex Travel: Travel stipend included Work facilities: Workstation at the Conservation Institute Research support: Research assistance included Healthcare: Available healthcare option Professional experience: At least seven years Application proposal: Maximum five typed, double-spaced pages Abridged CV: Maximum five typed, single-spaced pages Selected bibliography: Maximum two typed, single-spaced pages Application deadline: October 1, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. Los Angeles time (GMT-7) Decision notification: March or April 2027 Application method: Getty Foundation Grant Portal Conclusion The Getty Conservation Guest Scholars Program 2026 offers established cultural heritage conservation professionals an opportunity to dedicate three months to independent research within the Getty s internationally recognized research environment. With a $21,500 grant , accommodation, travel support, a workstation, research assistance, and access to Getty s collections and intellectual community, the program provides significant support for professionals seeking to develop research that can advance conservation practice. The opportunity is particularly suited to experienced practitioners and researchers with at least seven years of professional experience and a strong record of publications and other contributions to cultural heritage conservation. Applicants should focus on developing an original and clearly defined research project, demonstrating a practical methodology, explaining the project s potential impact, and making a compelling case for why Getty s resources are essential to the work. Applications are currently open, and the deadline is October 1, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. Los Angeles time (GMT-7) . Prospective applicants should carefully review the requirements and begin preparing their proposal, CV, and bibliography well in advance of the deadline. For more OFY Grant opportunities VISIT HERE. title: EMUNI University Master’s Programmes 2026/27: Study Mediterranean Geopolitics, Geoeconomics, Business and Digital Law in Slovenia
summary: The Euro-Mediterranean University (EMUNI) in Koper, Slovenia, is inviting applications for its 2026/27 master’s degree programmes , including two highly relevant programmes for students and professionals interested in international affairs, geopolitics, business, law, technology and global economic transformation. The two programmes are: Master’s in Mediterranean Geopolitics and Geoeconomics Master’s in Business and Digital Law Both programmes are delivered by EMUNI University in Koper, Slovenia , and provide an international academic environment designed to prepare graduates for careers that increasingly require an understanding of complex global political, economic, legal and technological developments. The Mediterranean Geopolitics and Geoeconomics programme focuses on international relations, geopolitics, global power competition, resources, trade, migration, security, diplomacy, regional studies and geoeconomics. The Business and Digital Law programme focuses on the legal challenges emerging from modern business and digital transformation, including artificial intelligence, data protection, blockchain, cryptocurrencies, financial technology, digital contracts, corporate law and technology regulation. Both programmes last two years , carry 120 ECTS , are taught in English and begin in October 2026 . EMUNI University Master’s Programmes 2026/27 at a Glance Feature Mediterranean Geopolitics and Geoeconomics Business and Digital Law University Euro-Mediterranean University (EMUNI) Euro-Mediterranean University (EMUNI) Location Koper, Slovenia Koper, Slovenia Duration 2 years / 4 semesters 2 years / 4 semesters Credits 120 ECTS 120 ECTS Degree Master of Arts LL.M. / Master of Laws Study mode Full-time, blended learning Full-time, blended learning Start October 2026 October 2026 Tuition €5,900 per academic year €5,900 per academic year Language English English International applicants Eligible Eligible Scholarships Competitive partial scholarships may be available Competitive partial scholarships may be available 1. EMUNI Master’s in Mediterranean Geopolitics and Geoeconomics The Master’s in Mediterranean Geopolitics and Geoeconomics is an interdisciplinary programme designed for students who want to understand how political power, economics, resources, geography, security, technology and international relations interact across the Mediterranean and the wider world. The programme is particularly relevant at a time when global power structures are rapidly changing. Students examine the relationship between states, regional powers, international organisations, businesses and non-state actors, while developing the ability to analyse geopolitical developments and translate complex information into practical policy, diplomatic, business and strategic recommendations. The programme is directed by Assist. Prof. Luka Juri . Programme Structure The programme consists of: 4 semesters 2 academic years 120 ECTS 15 core courses 2 elective courses A master s thesis The programme is delivered through full-time blended learning . According to the programme information, the first semester is online, while the second, third and fourth semesters are conducted on-site. The study location is Koper, Slovenia . What Students Learn in Mediterranean Geopolitics and Geoeconomics The programme combines political science, geography, economics, international relations, regional studies, diplomacy and strategic analysis. Students explore how: Great powers compete for influence. Regional powers shape political and economic developments. Maritime routes affect international trade. Ports and logistics networks influence strategic decisions. Energy corridors affect regional security. Data cables and digital infrastructure become geopolitical assets. Migration influences political relations. Demographic changes affect economic and political power. Narratives and identities influence conflict and cooperation. Artificial intelligence and cybersecurity are transforming diplomacy. Information warfare is changing international strategy. Natural resources affect geopolitical relationships. The programme therefore goes beyond traditional political science and provides students with an integrated understanding of political and economic power. Click HERE to learn more Mediterranean Geopolitics and Geoeconomics: Learning Outcomes Graduates are expected to be able to: Analyse regional and global power dynamics. Explain geopolitical developments clearly. Assess risks and opportunities for states, organisations and companies. Analyse Mediterranean and Eurasian geopolitical hotspots. Develop evidence-based policy options. Design strategies and scenarios. Understand international law and governance frameworks. Analyse security, trade, migration and resource-related issues. Communicate and negotiate in sensitive environments. Understand the role of culture, identity and narratives in international relations. These skills can be applied across government, diplomacy, international organisations, business, consulting, media, research and civil society. Mediterranean Geopolitics and Geoeconomics Curriculum Year 1 Course ECTS Foundations of Political Geography and Geopolitics 9 Research Methodology and Analytical Tools 6 Global Balance of Power and Spheres of Influence 6 Population, Power and Policy: The Geopolitics and Geoeconomics of Demographic Change 3 Regional Studies I – Mediterranean Civilization, Culture and Religious Thoughts 6 Emerging Global Challenges in Geopolitics 9 International Trade, Logistics and Transport 6 International Institutions, Law and Global Governance 6 Reading and Resolving Conflict: Negotiation Techniques and Cognitive Processes 3 Regional Studies II – Central and Eastern Europe, the Balkans and the Black Sea 6 Year 2 Course ECTS Geopolitics of Resources, Maritime Space and the Deep Sea 6 Geopolitical Geoeconomic Diplomacy in the Digital Era: Impact of AI, Blockchain Cybersecurity 9 Geopolitics and Narrative 6 Exogeography, Geopolitics and Geoeconomics of Outer Space 3 Regional Studies III – China and East Asia 6 Elective Course 1 8 Elective Course 2 8 Master Thesis 14 Elective Courses Students can select from specialised areas including: The West and the Muslim World Between Cooperation and Conflict Cultural Environments and Geoeconomics Central Europe and the Strategic Reordering of Eurasia Geoeconomics and Sustainable Development These electives allow students to deepen their knowledge in areas connected to their academic interests and career plans. Who Is the Mediterranean Geopolitics and Geoeconomics Programme For? The programme is particularly suitable for applicants with backgrounds in: International relations Political science Geography Economics Law History Sociology Related humanities and social-science disciplines It can also be relevant to professionals working in: Diplomacy Government Public administration NGOs International organisations Media Business Policy research Strategic consulting The programme is particularly suitable for people who want to understand how geopolitical and economic developments affect international organisations, governments, companies and societies. Admission Requirements for Mediterranean Geopolitics and Geoeconomics Applicants must generally meet one of the following academic requirements: A completed first-cycle degree equivalent to 180 ECTS or a three-year bachelor s degree in humanities, excluding languages, or social and behavioural sciences; or A previous higher-education professional study programme meeting the applicable requirements; or A qualification from another professional field equivalent in duration and scope. Applicants from other professional fields may be required to pass an admission interview covering: Political geography International relations Applicants with qualifications obtained outside Slovenia may be admitted following the applicable foreign-qualification recognition process. English Requirement Applicants generally need B2-level English proficiency under the CEFR . Acceptable evidence may include: IELTS 5.5–6.5 Cambridge FCE 160–179 TOEFL iBT 72–94 A comparable B2 certificate A bachelor s degree completed in English, accompanied by confirmation from the institution Native English speakers and candidates who completed their previous studies in countries where English is the language of instruction are considered to meet the requirement without submitting separate English-language proof. title: 2027 MEXT Scholarships at the University of Osaka, Japan | Undergraduate and Graduate Opportunities
summary: The University of Osaka (UOsaka) accepts international students who receive scholarships from the Japanese Government through the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT) . For the 2027 intake, MEXT scholarship opportunities are available at both undergraduate and graduate levels . Applicants can pursue the scholarship through two routes: Embassy Recommendation and University Recommendation . About the MEXT Scholarship The MEXT Scholarship is a Japanese Government scholarship programme for international students. At the University of Osaka, MEXT scholarship students can enter undergraduate programmes or pursue graduate-level research leading to master s or doctoral studies. At the graduate level, successful applicants usually begin as research students for approximately 6–12 months before proceeding to a master s or doctoral course after passing the relevant entrance examination. Study Levels The opportunity covers: Undergraduate programmes Master s programmes Doctoral programmes At undergraduate level, applicants may apply through Embassy Recommendation or University Recommendation. University Recommendation applicants must first pass one of the eligible undergraduate programmes and then be selected as MEXT student candidates. How to Apply There are two main application routes: 1. Embassy Recommendation Applicants are initially recruited and screened by the Japanese Embassy or Consulate General in their country. For graduate applicants, the process includes the embassy s first screening, followed by the process of obtaining a Letter of Acceptance from a Japanese university and subsequent MEXT and university procedures. 2. University Recommendation Under the University Recommendation route, the University of Osaka recommends candidates to MEXT. This route is generally connected to universities and research institutions with which the University of Osaka has relevant agreements or collaborative research relationships. September 1, 2026 Deadline Applicants who have already passed the first screening by the Japanese Embassy or Consulate General and wish to request a Letter of Acceptance from the University of Osaka must apply through the University s Admissions Assistance Desk (AAD) system. AAD Application Deadline for AY2027: September 1, 2026, Japan Time. Applications received from September 2 onward will not be accepted. It is important to note that this is the AAD Letter of Acceptance deadline , not a general deadline for all MEXT applicants. Documents Required for the AAD Application Applicants requesting a Letter of Acceptance through the AAD system must upload the required documents in PDF format, including: Application Form Field of Study and Research Plan Academic transcripts Certificate of graduation or degree Recommendation letter Medical certificate Language proficiency certificate, if available Passing Certificate of the First Screening issued by the Japanese Embassy or Consulate General Additional documents may apply depending on the applicant s circumstances. Documents that are not in Japanese or English must be accompanied by a translation into Japanese or English. Important Information for Applicants Approval through the AAD system does not itself mean that an applicant has received a Letter of Acceptance from a prospective supervisor. After receiving the AAD application result, applicants must complete additional procedures, which may include an interview and screening by the prospective supervisor. Applicants should therefore carefully follow the University s official instructions and the requirements of their prospective graduate school or programme. Where to Apply Applicants who have passed the first embassy screening and need to request a Letter of Acceptance should use the University of Osaka Admissions Assistance Desk (AAD) system. AAD Application Support System: https://www.ryumon.osaka-u.ac.jp/ Applicants should also consult the official MEXT Scholarship 2027 Application Guidelines and the University of Osaka s MEXT scholarship information before proceeding. Conclusion The 2027 MEXT Scholarship pathway at the University of Osaka provides international students with opportunities to pursue undergraduate and graduate studies in Japan through the Japanese Government s MEXT scholarship system. Prospective applicants should first determine which application route applies to them and carefully follow the relevant embassy, university and MEXT procedures. Graduate applicants who have already passed the first embassy screening should pay particular attention to the September 1, 2026 AAD deadline for requesting a Letter of Acceptance .
